title: OpenAI Apologises for AI Breach in Australia
content:
This comes after PM Anthony Albanese subsequently expressed “extreme concern” to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and criticised the company for taking “way too long” to notify Australian authorities.

OpenAI has apologised to the Australian government after one of its AI models gained unauthorised access to government systems during an internal training and evaluation exercise.

The company also disclosed that its models accessed systems operated by three other Australian government agencies.

“We are sorry and working to do better in the future,” OpenAI said in a statement published on September 28. “We also should have handled our response better.”

The most serious incident involved Services Australia’s Medicare Statistics Reporting Service in June.

An experimental internal model was tasked with finding government spending per person on medicines for skin conditions in Victorian communities.

After struggling to obtain the information, the model found a way to gain non-public access to the service, ran commands, retrieved internal files and credentials, accessed technical information and source code, and wrote files to an internal server.

OpenAI said it found no evidence that the model accessed individual patient or client records. The company said the model was not authorised to access the service or carry out the subsequent activity.

Three other agencies were also affected. At the NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research, a model accessed the public Crime Mapping Tool and made API and website metadata requests.

The system returned application configuration, operational jobs, logs and website metadata, but individual crime records were not accessed.

At Victoria’s Department of Health, OpenAI agents discovered an exposed access key and retrieved reporting configuration and aggregate survey statistics from a Victorian Agency for Health Information system. OpenAI said individual medical records and identifiable survey responses were not accessed.

At the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare (AIHW), agents retrieved aggregate statistics using third-party browsing and download services.

OpenAI said attempts to bypass access controls were unsuccessful and that the material appeared to have been publicly available.

The activity occurred in June but was disclosed only this month.

OpenAI said its review began after the separate Hugging Face incident in July and identified the Australian activity in mid-August.

It notified Services Australia and Victoria’s Department of Health on September 10, BOCSAR on September 18 and AIHW on September 24.

OpenAI acknowledged that it should have shared preliminary findings sooner.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese subsequently expressed “extreme concern” to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and criticised the company for taking “way too long” to notify Australian authorities.

The company’s Chief Strategy Officer Jason Kwon is scheduled to appear before Australia’s Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence next month.

He also announced that the incident would be referred to the Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, while the government would examine potential law-enforcement and legislative responses.

OpenAI said it has since strengthened network restrictions and monitoring, blocked live internet access in research environments and introduced human-review alerts.

It has also paused training and evaluation involving tool use for its most capable models until additional safeguards are in place.

In Australia, OpenAI will provide technical assistance to affected agencies, support cyber-defence efforts through its $1 billion Daybreak for Frontline Defenders fund and establish an Australian taskforce with independent experts.

The company has also committed to a range of measures to safely evaluate and release newer AI models, by slowing down the pace of training and establishing better frameworks to report safety incidents.

The company also recently scrapped its plans to release the GPT-6.1 Astra, citing safety concerns, which would otherwise be the successor to its most powerful model available to public, the GPT-6 Astra.

title: NVIDIA Approves Record $150 Bn Share Buyback as AI Boom Fuels Cash Generation
content:
NVIDIA’s latest addition to its share buyback programme takes the total authorisation to $235 billion.

NVIDIA’s board has approved an additional $150 billion for its share buyback programme, making it the largest single buyback authorisation increase in history, as the AI chipmaker continues to generate substantial cash from demand for its processors.

The company had previously announced an $80 billion share repurchase authorisation in May.

The new authorisation takes NVIDIA’s remaining buyback capacity to $235 billion, surpassing Apple’s previous $110 billion record. The company expects to execute the share buyback through fiscal year 2028.

“Our cash generation gives us the capacity to invest in the technologies that advance this transformation and return capital to shareholders,” NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement released by the company.

The announcement comes as NVIDIA continues to benefit from demand for chips used to train and run AI models. The company has forecast around 70% revenue growth for FY28, signalling continued confidence in demand for AI infrastructure.

The company ended its July quarter with $22.44 billion in cash and cash equivalents, as it continues to generate significant cash from its AI business.

NVIDIA’s shares were up 1.68% at the close of trading on September 28, trading at $228.86 apiece on Nasdaq. Over the last six months, its shares were up over 38%.

title: Kavitha Srinivasulu Joins Persistent Systems as Chief Cyber & AI Security Officer
content:
Srinivasulu will oversee AI security, risk advisory, and cybersecurity and work across leadership teams at Persistent Systems.

Kavitha Srinivasulu has joined Persistent Systems as Vice President – Chief Cyber & AI Security Officer, she announced on LinkedIn. Her remit covers cybersecurity, AI security, risk advisory, security engineering, and digital transformation.

Srinivasulu will work with customers, C-suite executives, and leadership teams to help “organisations navigate emerging technology risks” and use AI with security, resilience and trust in focus.

Before joining Persistent, Srinivasulu worked at Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), where she served as Programme Director, Cybersecurity and Data Privacy, with a focus on process optimisation and digital transformation.

Srinivasulu has more than 20 years of experience spanning BFSI, retail, manufacturing, healthcare, IT services and telecommunications, with previous roles at Wipro, Bank of America, Verizon, AstraZeneca alongside TCS.

Her appointment comes as enterprises expand agentic AI use across business and technology environments, increasing the need for security controls around AI systems. Anthropic's Mythos has also accelerated vulnerability discovery, creating new challenges for security teams as AI-assisted security research expands.

IT services companies are also incorporating cybersecurity into broader enterprise AI deployments, with Wipro using ServiceNow's AI platform capabilities for cybersecurity incident response and governance as part of its expanded partnership.

Srinivasulu said she would focus on enabling “secure transformation, trusted innovation and sustainable business value in the AI era.”

title: IBM, Yotta Launch Sovereign Agentic AI Platform for Enterprise Workflows
content:
The platform combines IBM’s AI-agent technology with Yotta’s sovereign cloud infrastructure to help organisations deploy and govern AI agents.

IBM and Yotta Data Services have launched the Sovereign Agentic AI Platform for Indian organisations, combining IBM’s enterprise AI capabilities with Yotta’s sovereign AI cloud infrastructure.

Built using IBM watsonx Orchestrate and deployed on Yotta’s Shakti Cloud, the platform is designed to help organisations deploy, run, and govern AI agents at scale while keeping data, inference, operations, and governance controls within India. It brings together AI-agent orchestration, GPU infrastructure, model development, and inference capabilities, with the platform available through Yotta’s Panvel and Greater Noida cloud regions.

IBM watsonx Orchestrate acts as an agentic control plane for securing, governing, and managing AI agents, while Shakti Cloud provides the compute, GPU infrastructure, networking, security, and operational capabilities required for enterprise AI workloads.

“With regulations evolving in India, digital sovereignty and open-source models are becoming a defining requirement for organisations as they scale AI from pilots to production. The priority is no longer just what AI can do, but how securely, transparently and compliantly it can be deployed,” Sandip Patel, Managing Director, IBM India and South Asia, said in a statement.

IBM and Yotta said the offering combines Yotta’s sovereign AI infrastructure with IBM’s enterprise AI and agentic AI capabilities.

“India’s AI journey requires organisations to have control not only over their data, but also over the infrastructure, compute, models, inference, and operations that power AI. Yotta’s Shakti Cloud and Shakti Studio provide this sovereign AI foundation, while IBM brings its enterprise AI and agentic AI capabilities to help organisations move from experimentation to production,” added Sunil Gupta, Co-founder, MD and CEO, Yotta Data Services.

Organisations can use the platform across workflows including security operations, document processing, and HR automation, among others.

CEO Bilal El Alamy argues that the bigger gap in AI is user adoption, not compute, as open-weight models offer companies a cheaper path to self-hosted AI.

Pyratz Corp, an Euronext-listed AI-native venture builder, has invested in Moonshot AI, the Chinese AI lab behind Kimi AI models, at a $30 billion valuation.

In an exclusive interview with AIM, Pyratz CEO Bilal El Alamy says the company “federated a syndicate of $10 million” for the investment. He adds that the investment reflects a broader bet on open-weight AI, self-hosted models, and a more decentralised AI ecosystem.

Unlike a traditional venture capital fund, Pyratz invests from its own balance sheet rather than managing capital on behalf of third-party investors, giving it greater flexibility over where it invests. This gives it greater flexibility over where it invests, including in companies and regions that may fall outside the usual constraints of a traditional fund.

El Alamy did not disclose Pyratz’s exact stake, saying the investment thesis matters more than the size of the ticket.

Moonshot AI has raised $7.27 billion to date, according to Tracxn. The company’s largest fundraise was $3.5 billion in July this year.

Pyratz was already a user of Kimi internally. El Alamy says the company has been building products to help entrepreneurs test and grow ideas faster and has integrated Kimi into those products.

The biggest attraction, however, is the economics of running the model.

“What we like about Moonshot is that it’s the cheapest model to self-host,” El Alamy says.

He compares the infrastructure cost of self-hosting an OpenAI model with Kimi. According to him, running an OpenAI model could cost around $30,000 a month in infrastructure, while Kimi can cost less than $5,000.

“Models like Kimi that are open-weight, efficient in terms of size and token consumption are very good models to start experiencing with AI,” he notes.

The company’s latest model, Kimi K3, has also made Moonshot a more serious commercial contender. Released in July, the 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model posted competitive results against leading proprietary models in third-party evaluations.

Moonshot is also reportedly in talks with Microsoft, Amazon and Google to host K3 on their cloud platforms, potentially creating a new distribution channel for a Chinese open-weight model outside China.

The investment also builds on Pyratz’s existing AI portfolio. Pyratz is also a shareholder in Paris-based AI startup Mistral AI, but El Alamy described the Moonshot investment as complementary rather than competitive.

“Mistral is developing a neocloud business where they’re open to basically hosting any type of open-weight model,” he says. He sees the Moonshot investment as complementary to that business.

El Alamy argues that Moonshot is undervalued relative to its commercial performance.

“Kimi is undervalued because Kimi has really amazing revenue KPIs,” he says, adding that Moonshot generates more revenue than Mistral while having a similar valuation.

El Alamy shares that Kimi has reached $1 billion in annual recurring revenue. “The thesis is that open-weight models are going to become more and more mainstream,” he adds.

He believes open-weight models will bring greater decentralisation to AI power because companies can run them on their own infrastructure rather than depending entirely on providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic.

El Alamy also points to growing usage of open-weight models, claiming that open-weight models accounted for 63% of AI tokens in the previous month.

Moonshot is also continuing with plans for a public listing in Hong Kong. El Alamy says the company is targeting the first half of 2027 for the IPO.

Moonshot confidentially filed for a Hong Kong IPO in September, targeting a potential $3 billion raise. The company was valued at around $50 billion at the time, after raising more than $5.5 billion, Reuters reported.

For Pyratz, the Moonshot investment combines a public-market opportunity with a longer-term thesis around open-weight models, self-hosted AI and a more decentralised AI ecosystem.

El Alamy dismisses calls from AI leaders including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for a slowdown in AI development, describing them as a “marketing gimmick”.

He argues that the industry should prioritise expanding AI adoption rather than spending heavily to push model performance further. According to El Alamy, only around 5–7% of people globally are actively using AI.

He also acknowledges the risks associated with open-weight models, including the possibility of malicious actors using them to develop biological weapons. But he says that concentrating AI capabilities among a small number of companies presents its own risks.

“We don’t want to have one entity or two entities that centralise all the AI power in the world,” he notes.

The investment also gives Pyratz exposure to China’s AI ecosystem at a time when access to advanced NVIDIA GPUs remains constrained by US export controls.

El Alamy says Chinese and other Asian AI companies have responded by becoming more efficient in how they train models.

He also says Chinese AI companies are renting compute from neocloud providers, allowing them to access infrastructure without directly owning the chips.

“They cannot buy chips, but they have access to compute,” he says.

El Alamy expects compute availability to increase as countries invest in energy infrastructure and data centres. He suggests Chinese AI companies could increasingly work with infrastructure providers across Japan, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and India.

title: HCLSoftware to Acquire Robotiq.ai, Add RPA to Agentic AI Platform
content:
HCLSoftware plans to acquire Croatia-based Robotiq.ai, adding RPA capabilities to HCL UnO Agentic for enterprise task execution.

HCLSoftware, the software business division of HCLTech, will acquire Croatia-based robotic process automation (RPA) company Robotiq.ai for an enterprise value of €9 million (~₹98 crore), adding RPA capabilities to its HCL UnO Agentic orchestration and automation platform.

The acquisition will allow HCL UnO Agentic to automate tasks in enterprise applications where application programming interfaces (APIs) are unavailable or insufficient, HCLSoftware said. The transaction is expected to close in November 2026.

Based in Zagreb, Robotiq.ai provides an enterprise RPA platform used in large banks, insurance groups, and telecom providers. The company said the platform includes ISO-certified security, audit logs, and flexible deployment options.

“Enterprises are looking beyond AI experimentation toward production-scale automation that is secure, governed and reliable,” Kalyan Kumar, President, HCLSoftware, said in a statement.

Agentic automation is also increasingly combining AI agents with software robots and human oversight across enterprise processes.

Video conferencing platform Zoom has also been expanding its agentic AI platform towards workflow execution. In March, it added capabilities for custom AI agents to retrieve information, automate tasks, and orchestrate workflows across third-party systems including Salesforce, Slack, and ServiceNow. Zoom's platform expansion followed a similar move towards workflow orchestration.

The acquisition also comes as HCLTech has expanded its generative AI work. Earlier this year, it expanded its collaboration with Gemini Enterprise and Gemini models to build custom AI agents.

title: Coforge Appoints Akhil Gupta as Chairperson for 5 years
content:
Coforge has appointed former Bharti Enterprises Vice Chairman Akhil Gupta as its Chairperson and Non-Executive Independent Director for five years.

Coforge has appointed Akhil Gupta as the Chairperson and Non-Executive Independent Director of the company, effective September 29. His appointment will be for five years.

Gupta, the former Vice Chairman of Bharti Enterprises, currently chairs the boards of 360 ONE WAM and Bharti AXA Life Insurance. He also serves on the boards of Zepto, Snapdeal, Eutelsat Communications and Lodha Developers. A chartered accountant, Gupta has more than 40 years of professional experience and completed the Advanced Management Program at Harvard Business School in 2002.

The appointment comes as Coforge expands its AI-led services business, with its AI strategy centred on generative AI, agentic AI and AI-enabled delivery.

Vivek Sharma, Non-Executive Independent Director and interim Chairperson, said the company conducted a global search for the position with executive search firm Egon Zehnder. The process began with 60 candidates before Gupta emerged as the unanimous choice of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) and the board.

“We are very excited to onboard an exceptional candidate as the Chairperson of Coforge,” Sharma said. He added that the search focused on governance experience, professional expertise and strategic perspectives.

Sudhir Singh, CEO and Executive Director of Coforge, said Gupta had been instrumental in helping Bharti Enterprises navigate multiple business shifts and welcomed him as Coforge moves into what he described as an AI-led era.

“Gupta was instrumental in Bharti Enterprises successfully navigating multiple business shifts during his watch and association with Bharti Enterprises,” Singh said.

Coforge reported a 31% year-on-year increase in revenue to ₹3,986 crore in Q2 FY26, while profit after tax rose 86% to ₹376 crore. The company’s Q2 FY26 performance came as it continued to expand its business.

Gupta has received several industry awards, including the EY Entrepreneur of the Year Award, the CA Lifetime Achievement Award and the CA Global Achiever Award from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI). He has also served as President of the Telecom Sector Skill Council and former Chairman of the Digital Infrastructure Providers Association.

title: Anthropic Lost $42 Billion in 2025: Report
content:
Anthropic spent $7.33 billion on computing and infrastructure during the year, about 3x its 2024 spending and more than half of its total operating expenses.

Anthropic reported a net loss of nearly $42 billion in 2025, according to its initial public offering (IPO) prospectus seen by Reuters.

The loss included a roughly $34 billion accounting charge linked to the increased estimated value of financing instruments that could eventually convert into Anthropic shares, rather than money the company spent.

Excluding those accounting effects, Anthropic’s operating loss widened to $8.06 billion in 2025 from $2.98 billion a year earlier. At the same time, revenue grew roughly 12-fold to nearly $4.6 billion.

The company spent $7.33 billion on computing and infrastructure during the year, about three times its 2024 spending and more than half of its $12.65 billion in total operating expenses.

AIM has reached out to Anthropic for a comment.

The prospectus also reportedly shows the scale of Anthropic’s planned infrastructure commitments.

The company expects to spend $518 billion on cloud, computing, and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.

It had $20.28 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments as of December 31, according to the filing.

Anthropic is reportedly seeking a public-market valuation of more than $2 trillion, more than double its estimated $965 billion valuation in May.

Its IPO follows OpenAI’s confidential filing for a US listing in June, and the report added that Anthropic’s offering could be delayed until after the November US midterm elections.

The filing also flags customer concentration as a risk. Nearly a quarter of Anthropic’s revenue came from two customers in 2025, while the company said many of its largest customers were not bound by long-term contracts and could reduce or stop spending.

The financial disclosure comes as Anthropic faces a parallel debate over the risks of increasingly capable AI systems. CEO Dario Amodei recently called for greater caution around the pace of AI development and recently told the UN Security Council that poorly managed AI could pose a risk to humanity.

title: Anthropic Launches Claude Sonnet 5.5 With 30% Lower Costs Per Task
content:
The new model costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, while Anthropic says it requires fewer tokens to complete the same tasks.

Anthropic has launched Claude Sonnet 5.5, the second model in its Claude 5.5 family, with improvements in coding, knowledge work and computer use.

Claude Sonnet 5.5 is available across Anthropic's platforms as well as Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure. Developers can access the model through the Claude Platform using claude-sonnet-5-5.

The AI company said Sonnet 5.5 generates outputs more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and can cost up to 30% less per task.

Sonnet 5.5 costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, while cache reads cost $0.20 per million tokens. Opus 5.5, by comparison, costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens.

Anthropic said Sonnet 5.5 requires fewer tokens per task than Sonnet 5, reducing the overall cost of running workloads despite retaining the same token pricing as its predecessor.

Sonnet 5.5 is positioned as a lower-cost alternative to Claude Opus 5.5 for everyday tasks, bug fixing and creating documents, slides and spreadsheets. Anthropic said Claude Haiku 5.5, which will target high-volume and cost-sensitive applications, will be launched in the coming weeks.

On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which evaluates models on agentic coding tasks, Sonnet 5.5 scored 70.6%, compared with 10.3% for Sonnet 5 and 66.4% for Opus 5.5.

Anthropic said the improvement also shows up in the cost of running coding tasks. At Medium effort on Terminal-Bench 4.0, Sonnet 5.5 exceeded Sonnet 5’s best score while costing less than one-tenth as much per task.

The model also closed the gap with Opus 5.5 on knowledge-work benchmarks. On GDPval-AA v2.1, Sonnet 5.5 scored 1,844, compared with 1,846 for Opus 5.5 and 1,449 for Sonnet 5.

On OSWorld 2.1, a computer-use benchmark, Sonnet 5.5 scored 80.1%, compared with 81.8% for Opus 5.5 and 57% for Sonnet 5. On Humanity’s Last Exam with tools, it scored 64.5%, against 67.7% for Opus 5.5.

However, Anthropic said benchmark scores capture only part of a model’s capabilities and that Opus 5.5 remains stronger for complex, open-ended tasks that require sustained judgement.

The company has also added cybersecurity safeguards similar to those used for Opus 5.5. Higher-risk cybersecurity requests can fall back to Sonnet 5, while users can continue to use the model for routine software development tasks.

title: AMD Acquires World Labs for $8.2 Bn, Fei-Fei Li to Join as Chief Scientist
content:
The deal brings World Labs’ spatial intelligence research into AMD, with the companies working towards an open AI ecosystem.

AMD has agreed to acquire AI research company World Labs in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $8.2 billion, bringing AI researcher Fei-Fei Li into AMD as Executive Vice President and Chief Scientist.

The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. Li will report directly to AMD CEO Lisa Su, while World Labs co-founders Justin Johnson and Ben Mildenhall will continue leading the team within AMD.

The deal gives AMD access to World Labs’ research in spatial intelligence and world models that will help understand, generate, and simulate three-dimensional environments.

AMD said the technology will help it better understand how AI workloads are evolving across areas including reasoning, robotics, simulation, and physical AI.

“Building the compute platforms for the next generation of AI requires a deep understanding of how models are evolving,” Su said in a statement.

“Fei-Fei and the World Labs team bring exceptional research leadership and model expertise. Together, we can use that insight to develop the hardware, software, and systems that will power the next generation of AI and strengthen the open AI ecosystem.”

The acquisition follows a technical partnership between the two companies that began last year. World Labs said the work initially centred on training and inference optimisation on AMD GPUs.

“As our teams worked together, we realised it would be a natural fit to bring together our AI ecosystem of software and hardware, foundation models, and applications,” World Labs said.

Li said the move will take World Labs closer to the hardware needed to scale its research.

“Without having a focused hardware effort, AI is hobbled in efficiency. And scale. And for our purposes, remains trapped in the digital world,” Li wrote in a post on X.

World Labs was founded in 2024 by Li, Johnson, Mildenhall, and Christoph Lassner. The company emerged from stealth in September 2024 with $230 million in funding and has since built models focused on spatial and physical intelligence.

In February, World Labs raised another $1 billion from investors including AMD, Nvidia, Autodesk, Emerson Collective, Fidelity Management & Research Company, and Sea. Autodesk invested $200 million in the round.

The company did not disclose its valuation, although Bloomberg had earlier reported that World Labs was deliberating another fundraise at a valuation of about $5 billion.

World Labs’ first product, Marble, uses its 3D world models to generate persistent and spatially coherent environments from images, video, text, and 3D layouts. The company says it is developing its models for applications spanning robotics, scientific discovery, creativity, and virtual worlds.

The acquisition also adds to AMD’s push to build an AI stack spanning chips, software, systems and models.

AMD acquired Finnish AI lab Silo AI for $665 million in 2024, with the company’s researchers working on AI models and software for AMD hardware. It also completed its $4.4 billion acquisition of ZT Systems in March 2025, adding expertise in AI infrastructure and rack-scale systems.

The World Labs deal takes that strategy further into model research. AMD said the company’s expertise will give it insight into emerging AI workloads and help shape future hardware, software, and systems.

Li will lead the research organisation alongside Johnson and Mildenhall after the transaction closes. The combined teams will work towards what the companies describe as an open AI ecosystem covering hardware, software, platforms, foundation models, and applications.

title: AI Needs $6 Tn Annual Revenue by 2031 to Justify Compute Spending: Bain Report
content:
Bain expects new AI products across autonomous systems, robotics, physical AI, and other emerging applications to drive $4.2 trillion in additional revenue.

The global AI industry will need to generate about $6 trillion in annual revenue by 2031 to support the infrastructure investment required to meet growing compute demand, according to Bain & Company’s seventh annual Global Technology Report.

Bain estimates that existing AI applications across consumer and enterprise markets could generate $1.2 trillion to $1.8 trillion in annual revenue. The remaining $4.2 trillion will need to come from new AI-driven products and markets.

“The debate today is fixated on employee productivity. The economics of AI infrastructure demand trillions in new revenue beyond productivity gains,” David Crawford, Chairman of Bain’s Global Technology practice, said in a statement.

Bain said the additional revenue could come from four areas: AI models replacing search engines and integrating advertising, autonomous systems such as cars, trucks and drones, physical AI including robotics and digital twins, and new applications such as drug discovery, mental health, and energy generation.

“What the industry needs is a wave of innovation that will dwarf what mobile and cloud unlocked,” Crawford said. He added that funding the infrastructure being built ahead of demand would require roughly 1% of additional annual global GDP growth.

The rise in AI compute demand has also changed the performance of hardware and semiconductor companies. Their market capitalisation grew at a 24% compound annual rate between 2020 and 2026, compared with 6% for software companies, Bain noted.

High-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging, and custom silicon are among the fastest-growing segments. Application-specific integrated circuits are also scaling as hyperscalers and AI companies develop chips for specific workloads.

Bain said custom chips are taking a larger share of data centre compute as training, inference, and agentic workloads reach volumes that can justify custom designs.

Supply risks are also changing procurement strategies. Companies are securing capacity across multiple locations and suppliers as natural disasters, geopolitical disruptions, and export controls create risks for semiconductor supply.

AI is also changing the cybersecurity landscape. Bain estimates that AI has reduced the time required for a typical cyberattack from about four weeks to 18 hours.

The growing use of AI agents adds another layer of risk, while existing approaches to monitoring software and AI vendors struggle to keep pace with frequent changes.

Bain’s CISO survey found that companies are increasing remediation budgets by double-digit percentages. Some are also redirecting 20–25% of cybersecurity staff from other work to address alerts generated by AI-powered scans.

The report identifies legacy platforms, network layers, and software-as-a-service vendors among the areas where companies are focusing remediation efforts.

Bain also identifies AI absorption speed, or how quickly companies can put AI into production, as a new competitive factor.

Leading AI labs are investing up to $9.75 billion in forward-deployed engineering to help enterprises integrate AI into their operations. Vendors are also developing application and infrastructure layers that connect AI models with enterprise systems.

Despite falling token prices, Bain does not expect large language models to follow a traditional commoditisation path.

“We see the more likely scenario as a continuum of frontier and mature models,” Crawford said. “New and unproven cases will initially favour frontier models, then likely migrate to lower-cost alternatives as the cases mature.”

Bain expects frontier models to remain focused on tasks where higher intelligence matters, while lower-cost and specialised models handle more established enterprise workloads.

The report also found that technology leaders expect AI to deliver a 148% improvement in release-cycle speed and a 95% increase in software developer productivity over the next one to two years. Current productivity gains range from 20% to 27%.

Bain said the gains from faster coding could create new bottlenecks in software review, coordination, quality, and governance, making changes to the wider software development lifecycle necessary.

title: Russia’s Sber Launches GigaChat 3.5 Reasoning to Take on Complex AI Tasks
content:
The Russian bank said GigaChat 3.5 Reasoning is the only Russian open-source model with a reasoning mode.

Sber has unveiled GigaChat 3.5 Reasoning, a new flagship model that can break complex problems into sequential steps, use external tools, check intermediate results and revise its approach before producing an answer.

The Russian bank said GigaChat 3.5 Reasoning is the only Russian open-source model with a reasoning mode. The model is already available to GigaChat users and developers, with developers able to integrate it into their products for free under the MIT licence. Sber said an API version for businesses will be available shortly.

The company says that unlike a conventional model that attempts to answer a question immediately, GigaChat 3.5 Reasoning can first create a plan, identify missing information, perform multiple actions, verify its intermediate conclusions and correct errors before returning the final response.

The reasoning mode is designed for tasks where a single answer or search is not enough, including finding inconsistencies between contract clauses, carrying out financial calculations and debugging complicated code.

“From now on, GigaChat can independently break down a task into stages, identify missing data, validate intermediate conclusions, and modify the solution if necessary,” said Anton Frolov, Senior Vice President and Head of GenAI Development at Sberbank. “This approach is crucial in agent-based scenarios, programming, and analytics — whenever the outcome depends on a whole sequence of decisions. This is a vital step toward AI that can independently build a path to a result, act proactively, and interact with other services. GigaChat is the only Russian model with a reasoning mode.”

The new version is particularly aimed at coding and agent-based tasks that require several actions to happen in sequence. Sber gives trip planning as one example. GigaChat can ask for missing details, select a flight and hotel, check whether the proposed itinerary fits the budget and then restructure the plan if it finds a discrepancy.

In following complex instructions, planning and code generation, GigaChat 3.5 Ultra Reasoning has approached the performance of leading global models, according to Sber. Its IFBench score increased from 44 to 77 points, while its Natural Plan score rose from 64 to 80. On Live Code Bench v6, its score increased from 56 to 85 compared with the version without reasoning.

The model is also designed to be more economical in its use of reasoning tokens. Sber said GigaChat 3.5 Reasoning uses significantly fewer tokens than leading open-source models with comparable answer quality.

In mathematical problem-solving, it uses an average of 37% fewer reasoning tokens than DeepSeek V4 Flash Preview.

Sber expects the reasoning model to be used across finance and banking for scenario forecasting and checking transactions against regulatory requirements. In legal services, it can search for inconsistencies in contracts and check documents against regulations or precedents.

Sber built GigaChat 3.5 Reasoning on top of GigaChat 3.5 Ultra, specifically training it to solve problems through sequential reasoning rather than simply producing an immediate response.

During training, the model was presented with mathematical and coding problems and taught to approach them through different solution paths. Automatic verification was then used to determine which reasoning approaches produced correct answers, with those paths reinforced during training.

The process was intended to teach the model not just how to arrive at an answer, but how to construct a sequence of actions. It also learned to decide when it should use an external tool and when it should return to an earlier step and revise its approach.

Under the hood, GigaChat 3.5 Reasoning uses Sber’s proprietary architecture with linear attention technology, which the company says makes the model more efficient when working with long contexts.

Sachin Tendulkar will share his experiences with ChatGPT and encourage more people to try it for their own interests and tasks.

Former Indian cricketer Sachin Tendulkar has partnered with OpenAI to explore how ChatGPT can be used in everyday life and share his experiences with the AI chatbot.

“I’m excited to announce my partnership with OpenAI. We have some interesting things coming up, and I can’t wait to share them with you,” Tendulkar said in a post on X.

The partnership is reportedly a multi-year collaboration to increase the use of AI in everyday activities in India.

It comes as OpenAI expands its presence in India. In February, the company said India had more than 100 million weekly ChatGPT users and announced its OpenAI for India initiative.

The programme includes partnerships around AI infrastructure, enterprise adoption, education, and workforce skills. OpenAI also plans to open offices in Mumbai and Bengaluru, in addition to its existing presence in New Delhi.

OpenAI has also expanded its association with Indian cricket. Earlier this month, the Board of Control for Cricket in India announced ChatGPT as an Associate Partner for India’s home cricket season for two seasons, running through March 2028.

Tendulkar has previously used generative AI publicly. In March 2025, he shared AI-generated images inspired by Studio Ghibli’s visual style during the trend that spread across India.

The Russian bank said GigaChat 3.5 Reasoning is the only Russian open-source model with a reasoning mode. The model is already available to GigaChat users and developers, with developers able to integrate it into their products for free under the MIT licence. Sber said an API version for businesses will be available shortly.

The company says that unlike a conventional model that attempts to answer a question immediately, GigaChat 3.5 Reasoning can first create a plan, identify missing information, perform multiple actions, verify its intermediate conclusions and correct errors before returning the final response.

The reasoning mode is designed for tasks where a single answer or search is not enough, including finding inconsistencies between contract clauses, carrying out financial calculations and debugging complicated code.

“From now on, GigaChat can independently break down a task into stages, identify missing data, validate intermediate conclusions, and modify the solution if necessary,” said Anton Frolov, Senior Vice President and Head of GenAI Development at Sberbank. “This approach is crucial in agent-based scenarios, programming, and analytics — whenever the outcome depends on a whole sequence of decisions. This is a vital step toward AI that can independently build a path to a result, act proactively, and interact with other services. GigaChat is the only Russian model with a reasoning mode.”

The new version is particularly aimed at coding and agent-based tasks that require several actions to happen in sequence. Sber gives trip planning as one example. GigaChat can ask for missing details, select a flight and hotel, check whether the proposed itinerary fits the budget and then restructure the plan if it finds a discrepancy.

title: NVIDIA Creates New Tool to Stop AI Agents From Going Rogue
content:
NVIDIA’s OpenShell creates a security boundary around agents running on Vera CPUs. It tracks what agents do and enforces rules governing their access to data, tools, and APIs.

NVIDIA has launched an open software and hardware reference platform to enforce security boundaries around AI agents.

The NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform combines OpenShell, an open-source security layer for AI agents, with Sentry, a monitoring system that runs on NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs.

The launch follows a series of incidents involving OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and others wherein AI agents broke out of testing environments and gained unauthorised access to real-world systems.

OpenShell creates a security boundary around agents running on Vera CPUs. It tracks what agents do and enforces rules governing their access to data, tools, APIs, and other services.

NVIDIA said OpenShell works with both open and closed AI models and can also be extended to third-party computing platforms, including those from Arm and Intel.

Sentry adds another layer of hardware-level protection. Running separately on BlueField-4 DPUs, it continuously monitors agent activity from an isolated system and can quarantine an agent if it tries to move beyond its permitted boundaries, NVIDIA said.

The system uses NVIDIA’s DOCA software to inspect agent requests and responses, verify their identity, track their activity, and enforce access controls over data, tools, APIs, and services.

“As we continue to discover the frontier of AI capabilities, we must accelerate discovery at the frontier of AI safety,” Jensen Huang, NVIDIA's CEO, said in a statement.

“NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform brings together industry, researchers and public-sector organisations to share best practices, align on evaluation methods and foster international cooperation.”

Several companies across the AI ecosystem have come together to support this initiative. This includes Microsoft, Anthropic, Oracle, SpaceX, IBM, and others. Notably, OpenAI was not included in the list of companies shared by NVIDIA.

Anthropic is integrating OpenShell and BlueField with Claude Managed Agents, while SpaceXAI is using the platform with Cursor coding agents and Grok models.

Scale AI is incorporating the technology into its agentic infrastructure, while Salesforce has integrated OpenShell with Slack so users can review agent activity and approve or reject requests for additional permissions.

The platform is also being adopted by companies including Microsoft, SAP, ServiceNow, Palantir, CrowdStrike, Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, Red Hat, Hugging Face, and Perplexity. Robotics companies including Figure, Gecko Robotics, and Skild AI are using OpenShell to add security controls to systems that allow AI agents to act in the physical world.

In light of frontier models breaking out of sandboxes and leaking sensitive information, Huang has dismissed calls for new AI-specific regulation, arguing that AI safety is primarily an engineering problem that requires appropriate security frameworks.

He has also criticised “exaggerated” narratives around AI, arguing that policymakers should not give in to speculative scenarios at the expense of addressing concrete engineering and security problems.

The Open Agent Safety Platform, including OpenShell and skills, is available through the NVIDIA developer resources and GitHub.

title: MongoDB CEO Joins Meta to Lead Enterprise AI Platform
content:
Meta announced Desai’s move alongside the launch of its Enterprise Platform.

MongoDB CEO Chirantan “CJ” Desai has stepped down from the database company to join Meta as Chief Enterprise Platform Officer, where he will report directly to CEO Mark Zuckerberg.

He will lead a newly formed business focused on selling Meta’s AI technology to enterprises.

Meta announced Desai’s move alongside the launch of its new Enterprise Platform.

Meta said the new unit will bring its AI models, agents and infrastructure into products for businesses and developers.

Its initial technology stack will include the Muse agent, Meta Business Agent, Muse API and Muse Code.

The company plans to build products businesses can deploy for areas including product development, customer engagement, decision-making, and day-to-day operations.

Desai joined MongoDB as CEO last November, succeeding Dev Ittycheria after the latter stepped down following 11 years leading the company.

Before MongoDB, Desai was President of Product and Engineering at Cloudflare and previously spent nearly eight years at ServiceNow, including as President and COO.

He has more than 25 years of experience across enterprise software, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity and AI.

MongoDB said Desai's resignation took effect on September 28 and was not related to any disagreement with the company's operations, policies or practices.

The company has appointed Ittycheria as interim President and CEO while its board searches for a permanent successor.

Meta's enterprise push extends its AI strategy beyond consumer products and advertising.

The company said it already works with millions of advertisers and hundreds of millions of businesses, and plans to use that existing business ecosystem alongside its models, agents and infrastructure to establish the new enterprise platform.

“We believe superintelligence will create significant new opportunities for all people and businesses,” wrote Zuckerberg in a post on X. “Meta Enterprise Platform will use our strengths that few other companies have: advanced models, leading agents, large-scale infrastructure, and years of working closely with many businesses.”

title: Infosys Plans to Move Up To 33% Workforce for Specialist AI Roles: Report
content:
Infosys has been expanding its AI capabilities and developing specialised roles within its workforce, including AI “builders” and “masters”.

Infosys reportedly plans to move between a quarter and one-third of its workforce into specialist roles as the Bengaluru-based IT services company expands its specialist talent base.

The plan was discussed by Infosys management during its three-day annual Americas confluence in Washington, DC, last week, where it met partners, advisers, and analysts, The Economic Times reported.

Infosys is also hiring talent from top Indian institutes and US campuses, often competing with AI labs for the same pool of engineers, according to people cited in the report.

AIM has reached out to Infosys for comment on the workforce transition and its specialist hiring plans.

Infosys has been expanding its AI capabilities and developing specialised roles within its workforce, including AI “builders” and “masters”. The company has also trained employees across functions to become AI-ready. In June 2025, Infosys said it had trained more than 2,75,000 employees in AI and generative AI.

The company has also invested in hiring employees with proven generative AI skills while upskilling its existing engineers.

The specialist-role plan comes alongside an earlier push to build a dedicated frontier engineering workforce. In July, CEO Salil Parekh said during the company’s post-earnings press conference, “Our plan is to have 6,000 frontier engineers over the next few years.”

Across the technology industry, companies are creating specialised positions such as Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), agent architects, and agent orchestrators as they build teams around AI systems and embed them inside enterprises.

title: India’s GCCs May Have Cut Up To 30,000 Jobs This Year as AI Reshapes Workforce: Report
content:
India’s GCC ecosystem currently employs around 2.4–2.5 million people across more than 2,100 centres.

India’s global capability centre (GCC) ecosystem has seen thousands of job cuts this year, with estimates ranging from 4,000–5,000 to as high as 25,000–30,000, as companies restructure their operations and push for AI-led productivity gains, as reported by Moneycontrol.

EIIRTrend CEO Pareekh Jain estimated the cuts at around 25,000–30,000, while 3AI’s Sameer Dhanrajani put the figure at 4,000–5,000. The reported reductions include around 600 roles at PayPal and 1,500 at Visa, along with cuts at ServiceNow and other GCCs.

The layoffs come as Indian GCCs take on larger technology, engineering, AI, and product mandates, signalling a shift from broad-based headcount expansion towards smaller teams with deeper technical capabilities.

India’s GCC ecosystem currently employs around 2.4–2.5 million people across more than 2,100 centres.

The workforce reductions come as AI changes the composition of work inside GCCs. Data cited by Moneycontrol shows that 17.7% of GCC work is commodity-based, while 38.1% is complex, while around 55% of the portfolio has some exposure to potential AI displacement. This does not mean 55% of jobs will disappear; rather, tasks within those roles could be redesigned or automated as companies change how work is performed.

Previously, Neeti Sharma, CEO, TeamLease Digital, told AIM, “While some impact comes from global headquarters restructuring, it’s not direct. Indian GCCs continue to gain higher-value work and are moving from volume hiring to skill-based, smaller, sharper teams focused on innovation.”

The distinction is becoming important as Indian GCCs take on more strategic functions. Centres are increasingly handling AI, engineering, and product responsibilities, including areas of enterprise decision-making previously concentrated at global headquarters.

This means headcount and strategic importance are not necessarily moving in the same direction. A GCC can reduce staffing in some functions while taking on more responsibility for products, engineering platforms, and AI systems. Companies are also continuing specialised hiring and establishing new centres, even as they become more selective about overall headcount.

title: India Launches AI-First Digital Stack to Connect Fragmented Tourism Ecosystem
content:
The National Digital Tourism Stack will connect tourism providers and travellers across digital platforms, with 1,000+ experiences already transacting on ONDC.

India has launched an AI-first digital infrastructure for tourism, with the Ministry of Tourism and Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) launching the National Digital Tourism Stack (NDTS) on World Tourism Day to connect destinations, tourism businesses, and travellers across multiple digital platforms.

The stack is designed to address fragmentation across India’s tourism ecosystem by bringing together homestays, attractions, guides, experiences, and transport services through common digital infrastructure. It will support AI-led travel discovery and planning, while allowing tourism providers to list their offerings and become discoverable across participating platforms.

The initiative is designed around 23,000+ tourism experiences and homestays, while 1,000+ tourism experiences, including 170 ASI monuments and 29 museums, are already transacting on the ONDC network.

“As travel discovery increasingly moves towards AI-led interfaces and personal digital agents, that infrastructure also needs to remain trusted and adaptable to new forms of traveller experience,” Karthick Prabhu, Vice President, Travel, ONDC, said in a statement.

The stack is being designed to support AI-led interfaces and personal digital agents for travel discovery and planning. The Ministry of Tourism has also outlined a “One ticket, One pass” vision to bring different parts of a traveller’s journey together through common digital infrastructure.

Trust is another core layer of the initiative, with the infrastructure envisaged to support provider credentials, reliable tourism information, service standards, ratings and reviews, and grievance mechanisms, according to the Ministry.

The Ministry will work with states and union territories to curate and validate tourism experiences as the programme expands. The initiative also aims to widen digital market access for smaller tourism businesses and lesser-known destinations.

title: Microsoft Revamps Copilot With Home, Code and Autopilot Capabilities
content:
Microsoft is also introducing usage-based billing for agentic workloads and tools to help organisations manage AI spending

Microsoft has unveiled a version of Copilot that brings Home, Code and Autopilot into the app, turning it from a conversational AI assistant into a platform for building solutions and running longer tasks.

Microsoft said the new Copilot will connect the tools people use at work with capabilities for building, customising and scaling AI.

Home will serve as the new starting point for Copilot, bringing Chat and Cowork together. It will also include Office in Copilot, giving users access to Word, Excel and PowerPoint within the Copilot experience.

Microsoft said users can ask Copilot to create or update documents, spreadsheets, and presentations while keeping them editable and synced with Office applications.

Code will allow users to build apps, trackers, dashboards, automations and workflows using natural-language instructions. Microsoft said Code is powered by the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot and runs in a sandboxed environment.

“Describe an app, tracker, dashboard, automation or workflow in natural language, and Copilot chooses an approach and builds it,” Microsoft said.

Code will start rolling out to Microsoft's Frontier programme at the end of September, with broader availability planned in the following weeks.

Autopilot, previously called Scout, is built to operate as a persistent agent that can continue working without a prompt. Microsoft said users can give it a name, role and goal, after which it can monitor channels, follow up on conversations and run recurring tasks.

For example, Microsoft said Autopilot could manage a supplier review process, including creating a schedule, preparing meetings and following up with stakeholders.

“Autopilot is cloud-hosted, so it keeps working while you sleep or your attention is elsewhere,” Microsoft said.

Autopilot will expand to private preview at the end of September.

Microsoft is also introducing Copilot Managed Runtime, which provides infrastructure for running code inside an organisation's Microsoft 365 environment.

The company said the runtime lets applications connect to live data while IT remains in control. It will support apps built with Cowork, Code and Copilot Studio, as well as third-party and pro-code development.

Microsoft is also expanding Copilot’s access to business data through Microsoft IQ. Fabric IQ will bring data from Power BI's semantic models into Copilot, while integrations with Dynamics 365 and Power Platform will add business data and workflows.

The company is also rolling out a new plugin registry where Microsoft, partner and custom-built plugins can be managed from a single catalogue.

The company is introducing different billing models for conversational and agentic workloads.

Microsoft said user subscription licences will cover everyday Copilot use, including Chat and Copilot within Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams. An ‘Auto’ system will select models based on accuracy, speed and cost.

Long-running agentic features such as Cowork, Code and Autopilot, along with frontier models including Astra and Fable, will use usage-based billing.

Microsoft is also adding FinOps capabilities that let administrators manage AI spending, control model access and track usage across their organisations.

The company said users will be able to view credit usage, remaining balances and usage history within Copilot.

Microsoft also previewed Today, a new command centre that will bring together information from email, calendars, Teams conversations, meetings and tasks. It will enter private preview in October.

The company is also bringing shared context to @Copilot in Teams, allowing Copilot to use the context and permissions of a channel, group chat or meeting when answering questions and preparing follow-up work.

title: White House Asks OpenAI, Anthropic to Hold Models From UK Testers: Report
content:
The request could affect AISI’s longstanding arrangement with leading AI labs, under which the UK institute has received pre-release access to frontier models for safety and security testing.

The White House has asked OpenAI and Anthropic not to provide new AI models to the UK’s AI Security Institute (AISI) until the systems have first been reviewed by the US government, according to a report by Politico.

The request was made by the Office of the National Cyber Director, with a US administration official saying Washington wants to assess the models and ensure US systems are secure before they are shared with partners

The request could affect AISI’s longstanding arrangement with leading AI labs, under which the UK institute has received pre-release access to frontier models for safety and security testing.

AISI was established in 2023 and has tested models from companies including OpenAI and Anthropic before public release.

AISI Director Henry de Zoete told a UK parliamentary committee earlier this month in a letter that the institute had not received Anthropic’s latest model, while noting that it retained pre-release access to some other advanced systems.

AISI had previously tested OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra ahead of its release, the report added.

The White House request comes as governments are increasing scrutiny of frontier models following incidents during safety evaluations.

AISI said last month that agents tested in a controlled cybersecurity exercise took 19 unsanctioned actions against real people and organisations across 10 of 122 test runs. Most of those actions involved Anthropic’s Mythos 5, while two involved OpenAI’s GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber safeguards disabled.

The dispute also comes as Washington and London are advocating different approaches to international AI safety coordination.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called for a “single set of global principles and standards”, while OpenAI this week called for the US to lead international technical standards for frontier AI, including coordinated evaluation and reporting.

The UK government, as quoted in the report, said AISI would continue working with the US, international partners and AI companies.

“These risks do not stop at national borders and no country can tackle them alone,” a government spokesperson said.

The scale of that infrastructure is also becoming a commercial asset.

title: Sarvam Launches Vision 2.1 With Improved Document Intelligence Across 22 Indian Languages
content:
Sarvam says the updated model delivers stronger table extraction, form field recognition, and handwritten text processing, while reducing hallucinations and inference costs.

AI startup Sarvam AI has launched Sarvam Vision 2.1, a document intelligence model with new capabilities for structured extraction, complex table parsing, and Indic handwritten text recognition. The company said the model achieves state-of-the-art results on its Indic OCR benchmark and the olmOCR-Bench, which evaluates how vision models convert complex PDF files into Markdown format.

Sarvam Vision 2.1 is available through Sarvam’s document intelligence APIs, including Digitize API for converting multi-page documents, tables, and handwritten content into structured text, and Extract API for extracting key-value pairs, tables, and form fields.

The company said the new model addresses gaps identified in the earlier version of Sarvam Vision launched in February this year, particularly in multi-page table extraction, key-value extraction from forms, and Indic handwriting recognition. It also includes changes to reduce hallucinations and inconsistencies in the model.

“Sarvam Vision 2.1 is a step change in terms of its new and improved capabilities,” the company said in a statement. “It achieves frontier performance on benchmarks, and is built for production workflows.”

On the official olmOCR-Bench, Sarvam Vision 2.1 scored 87.30, ahead of Infinity-Parser2 Pro at 86.10 and Opus 5 at 85.10. Sarvam Vision 1.0 scored 84.10 on the same benchmark.

On OmniDocBench v1.6, which evaluates text, table structure, and formula recognition, Sarvam Vision 2.1 scored 94.97. PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 led the benchmark with 96.01, followed by Sarvam Vision 2.1 and GLM-OCR at 94.71.

Sarvam also introduced an Indic OCR benchmark covering 22 Indian languages. It evaluates character and word accuracy using material from newspapers, brochures, textbooks, and historical writings dating from 1800 to the present.

Sarvam Vision 2.1 recorded 87.39% overall word accuracy on the benchmark, compared with 84.94% for Bodhan Indic-OCR and 79.35% for Gemini 3.6 Flash. Google Cloud Vision scored 71.76%, while GPT 6 Astra recorded 63.69%.

The company trained the model on both synthetic and real-world data for key-value extraction and Indic handwriting. Sarvam also carried out supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, or RLVR.

Sarvam said it has also optimised the inference stack to reduce the cost of serving the model. The API has been optimised for production workloads following feedback from users of the first version.

title: Oracle Moves to Shield Itself From Delays at New Mexico AI Data Centre: Report
content:
However, Oracle said Project Jupiter remains on schedule despite delays and regulatory hurdles affecting its power infrastructure.

Oracle has issued a force majeure notice to the developer of Project Jupiter, a large AI data centre campus in Doña Ana County, New Mexico, seeking to protect its contractual position if the facility is delayed, Bloomberg reported. Oracle is not seeking to exit the project but is seeking to defer certain payments if the campus fails to come online in 2028 as planned, people familiar with the matter reportedly said.

Force majeure provisions can provide contractual relief when events beyond a party’s control prevent or delay it from meeting its obligations.

In Oracle’s case, the notice comes amid delays and regulatory hurdles affecting Project Jupiter’s power infrastructure.

Oracle shares fell 3.5% on September 24 following reports of the notice, while Blue Owl, which owns Project Jupiter’s developer, closed 3.6% lower.

“Project Jupiter remains on our planned schedule. We are fully committed to New Mexico and confident in our path forward,” Oracle said in a statement on X.

The project was initially designed around 2.2GW of gas turbines, but New Mexico’s State Land Office rejected Energy Transfer’s requests for rights-of-way and a lease needed for a natural-gas pipeline serving the site, according to reports.

The pipeline route was reportedly subsequently changed, while its planned in-service date has been pushed to February 1, 2027, from August 15.

Oracle subsequently changed the power design, replacing the planned gas turbines and diesel generators with Bloom Energy fuel cells.

The campus is designed to handle about 2.45GW, while Bloom is contracted to provide 2.4GW of fuel-cell capacity, according to TechCrunch. A separate air-quality permit for the fuel-cell system is also pending.

Bloom said it remains committed to Project Jupiter and its contract with Oracle. “Oracle remains committed to Project Jupiter and its contract with Bloom to deliver 2.4 GW of fuel cell capacity,” the company said on X. “We are excited to execute Project Jupiter on Oracle’s planned timeline.”

Oracle also pointed to the scale of construction already under way. More than 3,600 construction workers are currently working on the campus, including more than 1,000 New Mexico residents, the company said. More than 900 workers joined the project in August alone, while construction crews have logged more than 2.8 million hours.

Oracle estimates that Project Jupiter will generate more than $4.7 billion in long-term economic impact for New Mexico. The company has previously said the estimate assumes the project's air permit and pipeline are approved as planned.

Blue Owl, whose unit STACK Infrastructure is developing Project Jupiter, said the notice does not change the project’s financial commitments. “This notice does not change the financial commitments to this multiyear project,” a Blue Owl spokesperson said as quoted by several media outlets.

Project Jupiter is part of Oracle’s broader infrastructure agreement with OpenAI. The 1,400-acre campus is one of the data centres being developed to provide computing capacity under the companies’ multiyear agreement.

The project has also been financed through about $18 billion in loans from a consortium of banks.

title: Google to Test AI Chips in Space With Project Suncatcher
content:
The mission will assess how Google’s TPUs handle radiation, vibration, and thermal extremes in low Earth orbit.

Google is preparing to launch a prototype satellite for the first orbital test of Project Suncatcher. The test will examine how Google Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) perform in space. It will fly on SpaceX’s upcoming Transporter-18 rideshare mission.

The satellite will collect data on hardware performance in orbit.

The first mission will focus on whether AI hardware can withstand spaceflight. Google will study the effects of vibration, acceleration, radiation, and temperature extremes. The company said the satellite will provide data for future missions.

“This first launch is about seeing what works, identifying points of failure, and applying those findings to future missions,” the company said in a blog post.

Google has already tested its TPUs against several conditions expected during the mission. A rocket journey to low Earth orbit lasts about 10 minutes. During launch, spacecraft can experience acceleration loads of up to 10g. Individual components can face forces reaching 50–100 g.

The team also tested Trillium TPUs against radiation at UC Davis’ Crocker Nuclear Laboratory. Researchers ran AI workloads during proton beam testing. They monitored errors such as bit flips and their impact on workloads. Google said initial results showed the TPUs could withstand radiation beyond a five-year space mission dose.

Cooling remains another challenge for the project. TPUs generate significant heat in a small area during operation. Space lacks airflow, so conventional cooling methods cannot work in a vacuum. Google is testing heat pipes and radiators to move heat away from the chips.

The company has tested its cooling technology inside a thermal vacuum chamber. The chamber simulates the thermal and vacuum conditions found in space. Google will use the orbital test to assess the new cooling system and refine future designs.

Google also plans to test communication between satellites. Future Suncatcher satellites could carry dozens of TPU chips and operate in clusters. The satellites will use lasers to communicate and maintain the bandwidth required for AI workloads.

The project faces a demanding communications challenge. Existing space laser systems usually support lower bandwidth across longer distances. Suncatcher requires high bandwidth across short distances between moving satellites. Google plans to test this system in 2027 with two satellites in orbit.

The company is presenting Suncatcher as a long-term research effort rather than an immediate space-based data centre deployment. Its early tests will determine whether the hardware, cooling systems, and satellite links can support the concept in orbit.

Google announced Project Suncatcher last year as a research programme for space-based machine learning infrastructure. The company is exploring whether satellite constellations could support scalable AI workloads. Low Earth orbit offers near-constant sunlight, which can generate up to eight times as much solar power as on Earth.

title: Genesys Wins ₹283 Cr World Bank-Funded Contract for Ahmedabad Digital Twin
content:
As part of the project, around 25 lakh properties will be surveyed, geocoded, and assigned unique digital identities

Genesys International Corporation has won a ₹283 crore World Bank-funded contract to build a 3D digital twin and spatial intelligence platform for Ahmedabad, in what the company describes as one of India’s largest city-scale digital twin initiatives.

The project will digitally map approximately 625 sq km of Ahmedabad and 25 lakh properties, creating a unified GIS platform covering land parcels, properties, roads, and critical civic infrastructure, including water, sewerage, and stormwater networks.

The initiative is part of the Gujarat Resilient Cities Partnership programme and is aimed at strengthening urban planning, infrastructure management, and civic service delivery.

The project is expected to take two and a half years to complete, followed by five years of operations and maintenance.

As part of the project, around 25 lakh properties will be surveyed, geocoded, and assigned unique digital identities.

Genesys will also develop an elevation model using orthophotography and establish 40 primary and 200 secondary survey control points to improve the accuracy of the city's spatial database.

The platform will bring property-level information and city infrastructure onto a common digital foundation, allowing municipal departments to access and work with the same spatial data.

A significant component of the project will be mapping Ahmedabad's underground civic infrastructure.

Existing water supply, sewerage, stormwater drainage, and cable networks will be surveyed and mapped, including their location and depth. The information will then be integrated into the central GIS database.

This could give civic agencies a unified view of both above-ground and underground infrastructure, potentially helping coordinate infrastructure projects, maintenance, and future urban development.

The Ahmedabad project expands Genesys' work in city-scale 3D mapping, combining surveying, GIS, artificial intelligence, and spatial data to create digital representations of urban environments.

Sajid Malik, Chairman and Managing Director, Genesys International, said the project goes beyond conventional digital mapping.

“Ahmedabad—like most Indian cities—is entering an important phase in its urban development, and the ability to understand the city as a connected, three-dimensional digital environment will be increasingly important. This project is not simply about a digital map; it is about building a high-precision digital representation of the city that brings together land, properties, roads, utilities and underground infrastructure on a common spatially intelligent platform,” he said.

This marks the beginning of using physical AI systems in urgent governance delivery.

The company said the resulting spatial intelligence platform could eventually support applications spanning infrastructure planning, utility management, property administration, mobility, disaster preparedness, and civic services.

For Ahmedabad, the project effectively creates a digital layer over the physical city—from individual properties and roads to infrastructure buried underground—that government agencies can use as a common reference for urban planning and delivery.

title: Databricks Acquires Row Zero to Bring Governed Spreadsheets to Genie
content:
The deal will let business teams analyse live enterprise data, build models and collaborate while keeping permissions, data lineage and agent actions auditable.

Databricks has acquired Row Zero, a spreadsheet platform built to connect business users and AI agents with live enterprise data.

The acquisition will add a spreadsheet interface to Genie, Databricks’ AI coworker for business teams. Users will be able to analyse data, build models, explore scenarios and collaborate through a spreadsheet while working with data governed through Databricks’ platform.

Row Zero will integrate with Databricks’ Genie Ontology, Unity Catalog and Unity Gateway. The company said the integration will let users move between Genie’s conversational interface and spreadsheets for tasks such as pivoting, modelling and visualisation.

“Genie is helping make every knowledge worker dramatically more productive and impactful. As more finance, operations, and go-to-market teams adopt Genie, incorporating a seamless spreadsheet experience is a must-have,” said Patrick Wendell, Co-founder and VP of Engineering at Databricks.

Spreadsheets remain widely used by business teams for financial modelling, analysis and decision-making. However, spreadsheet files often involve exported or duplicated data that can sit outside an organisation’s governance and security controls.

Databricks said Row Zero addresses this by connecting spreadsheets directly to live, governed data sources. Queries can respect user permissions, data can refresh from authoritative sources, exports can be restricted and results can be written back to data systems.

The integration also brings spreadsheets into the agent workflow. Row Zero provides agent tools that allow users to work with data through the spreadsheet interface, while keeping agent actions interpretable and auditable.

Row Zero supports formulas, pivot tables and keyboard shortcuts used in tools such as Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets. Its processing engine can work with billions of rows at interactive speeds, according to Databricks.

“We built Row Zero because we love spreadsheets but recognised they needed to seamlessly connect to enterprise-scale data with governance and security at the core,” said Breck Fresen, Founder and CEO of Row Zero.

“Joining Databricks accelerates our vision of giving business users the spreadsheet they deserve: secure, connected, scalable, and deeply integrated with AI agents,” Fresen added.

Row Zero was founded by former AWS and Tableau engineers. The team will join Databricks and continue working on Genie.

The spreadsheet platform will be available to Databricks customers across major cloud providers and will continue to support data sources outside Databricks.

title: Akamai Signs $11.6 Bn Cloud Deal With Anthropic
content:
The seven-year agreement will support Anthropic’s growing CPU workload demand, with the partnership potentially expanding to $20 billion.

Cloud and cybersecurity company Akamai has signed a seven-year agreement worth $11.6 billion with Anthropic to provide cloud infrastructure and software for the AI company’s growing CPU workloads.

The agreement could expand by another $9 billion, taking the total potential commitment to about $20 billion over the seven-year term.

Under the deal, Anthropic will use Akamai Cloud’s distributed infrastructure to support CPU workloads. Akamai said the agreement adds to more than $2.8 billion in multi-year Cloud Infrastructure Services commitments across its customer base announced earlier this year.

“Akamai has an unparalleled reputation for helping our customers achieve their business-critical goals and build the future,” said Tom Leighton, Co-founder and CEO of Akamai Technologies. “Our expanding global footprint, combined with our years of experience serving the world’s largest enterprises, positions us to be the infrastructure provider for secure and responsible AI applications and workloads.”

Akamai said the agreement will require about $5.5 billion in capital expenditure. The company expects to spend an additional $1.7 billion in 2026 to secure and pre-purchase supply chain components, including memory.

Akamai does not expect the deal to affect its 2026 revenue guidance.

As part of the agreement, Akamai has issued Anthropic a warrant to purchase non-voting convertible Series B Preferred Stock representing 7.7 million Akamai shares on an as-converted basis.

The warrant could represent about 5% of Akamai’s outstanding common stock. Around 2% is expected to vest in connection with the initial $11.6 billion commitment.

The remaining 3% is tied to the agreement's potential expansion. Each additional $3 billion purchase of cloud services, subject to mutually agreed terms, would result in the vesting of approximately 1% of Akamai’s common stock outstanding.

Akamai said its cloud platform provides compute across core and edge locations through a distributed network spanning thousands of points of presence.

The agreement comes as AI companies expand infrastructure spending beyond GPU computing to support the CPU workloads involved in running and operating AI applications at scale.

title: Windows Malware Uses 4 AI Models To Decide Its Next Move
content:
CLOSEDQUORUM can query DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral and Google Gemini, using their responses to select its next action instead of relying entirely on instructions from an attacker-controlled command-and-control server.

A Windows malware strain is using multiple AI models to determine its next move, delegating tactical decisions to AI models, rather than relying entirely on commands from an attacker-controlled server.

CLOSEDQUORUM, a Windows malware strain analysed by Cisco Talos, uses DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral and Google Gemini to vote on its next action, including stealing data, injecting code or establishing persistence. It can target Windows credentials, browser passwords and crypto wallets, but Talos has not observed a full attack, and the analysed sample contains placeholder API keys and a dummy Discord webhook.

A Windows malware strain called CLOSEDQUORUM uses multiple AI models to decide what to do on an infected computer. It can query DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral and Google Gemini, using their responses to select its next action instead of relying entirely on instructions from an attacker-controlled command-and-control server.

“Human operators are bound by attention, working hours, and cognitive load. An AI system capable of executing a phase of the attack chain can continue when the operator is no longer watching,” said Ryan Fetterman of Cisco Talos.

The models receive information about the compromised system and choose between four actions: Steal, Inject, Persist and Move. Steal can collect Windows credentials from LSASS memory, browser passwords and cryptocurrency wallet data. Inject supports techniques including process hollowing and Early Bird APC injection, while Persist can use Registry Run keys, scheduled tasks and WMI event subscriptions. Move is intended for lateral movement but is not implemented in the analysed version.

The AI models are not creating new attack techniques. They choose from capabilities already built into the malware, with the majority response determining what happens next.

The analysed sample contains placeholder API keys and a dummy Discord webhook, meaning it does not work as distributed. Evidence also links its developer to criminal forum activity dating to 2025. The finding demonstrates that AI models can be used to automate a bounded phase of an attack, but researchers have not confirmed its use in real-world attacks.
