title: US Biopharma Co Syneos Health Opens 137,000 Sq Ft Global Life Sciences and Technology Centre in Hyderabad
content:
The centre is Syneos Health’s largest facility in Asia and third-largest globally.

Syneos Health has opened a 137,000 sq ft Global Life Sciences and Technology Centre in Hyderabad, with an initial workforce of more than 700 professionals, as the US-based biopharmaceutical solutions company expands the city’s role as a global hub for life sciences, clinical research, technology, and AI.

The centre is Syneos Health’s largest facility in Asia and third-largest globally, and will bring together capabilities spanning clinical development, commercialisation, medical affairs, technology, AI, and corporate functions. The workforce is expected to expand over the coming years as the company builds specialised capabilities from Hyderabad for its global operations.

The facility comes as Hyderabad strengthens its position as a major healthcare and life sciences GCC destination. The city accounts for an estimated 20–23% of India’s healthcare-biotech GCC market, supported by Telangana’s broader ecosystem spanning APIs, bulk drugs, generics, CDMOs, vaccines, research, and drug discovery.

Syneos Health is positioning the Hyderabad centre as more than a traditional delivery centre, with global leaders, clinical and commercial specialists, technologists, and AI teams working from the city to support drug development and commercialisation for customers worldwide.

“Beyond building capabilities, we are bringing together leaders, experts and innovators who are helping redefine how work gets done, creating smarter approaches to drug development and commercialisation for customers around the world,” Tom Wollman, Head of Operational Excellence, Syneos Health, said in a statement.

Syneos Health’s expansion also adds to Hyderabad’s growing concentration of global contract research organisations. With Syneos Health’s presence, four of the world’s top five CROs now have operations in Hyderabad. Global healthcare and pharmaceutical companies including MSD, Sanofi, Bristol Myers Squibb, Eli Lilly and Amgen have also been expanding capabilities across Telangana’s life sciences value chain, spanning R&D, clinical development, data, technology and AI.

Telangana IT Minister D Sridhar Babu said Hyderabad’s existing life sciences and technology strengths create an opportunity to build AI-enabled healthcare capabilities.

“Hyderabad has built one of India’s strongest life sciences ecosystems and one of its deepest technology talent pools. The next opportunity is to bring these strengths together with AI,” D Sridhar Babu, Minister for Information Technology, Electronics & Communications, Industries & Commerce, and Legislative Affairs, Government of Telangana said.

“With an end-to-end ecosystem spanning APIs, bulk drugs, generics, CDMO, vaccines, research and discovery, and a growing concentration of global healthcare and biotech GCCs, Hyderabad has the talent and depth to become a global testbed for AI-enabled life sciences,” he added.

Syneos Health said the Hyderabad centre will serve as a strategic growth hub where teams across clinical, commercial, technology, and scientific functions collaborate on global projects.

“This is far more than a new office. It is a strategic hub where global leaders, clinical and commercial experts, and technologists and innovators are helping shape the future of healthcare, while delivering better outcomes for biopharmaceutical customers,” Jinu Jose, General Manager, India and Strategic Growth Hubs, Syneos Health, noted.

Meta has unveiled Muse Charm, a palm-sized AI device that gives users direct access to its Muse personal AI agent without opening a phone app.

The company announced the device at its Meta Connect event and said the device brings Muse’s “state-of-the-art real-time voice model” into a pocket-sized form factor and will have more details later this year.

According to a report from Bloomberg, Charm has a roughly 2-inch OLED touchscreen, built-in 5G connectivity and speakers and microphones.

It can be carried in a pocket, worn on a wrist strap or attached to a bag or keychain.

The device has front and rear cameras that are primarily intended to give Muse visual information for analysis and AI-assisted actions, rather than simply serving as conventional phone cameras.

The device runs a dedicated operating system and displays a virtual Muse character that users can customise, including its appearance, clothing and voice.

It can also play music and video and includes a USB-C charging port, although it does not support phone or video calls. Users will set up and synchronise the Charm through the Muse app on an iPhone or Android phone.

The device is slated to ship in December, although Meta has not announced a price.

Bloomberg also reported that the project began as a prototype and was developed in roughly nine months by Meta’s new design team, led by former Apple design executive Alan Dye, in coordination with the Muse team.

Internally, the prototype was reportedly called ‘Clawmagochi’, combining its Tamagotchi-like design with the team’s interest in the OpenClaw AI assistant.

The announcement comes as Meta expands Muse across its hardware portfolio. The company has said Muse will become the primary AI interface for its smart glasses, where it can handle tasks and interact with users through voice.

Muse is designed as a general-purpose personal AI agent that can carry out tasks on a user’s behalf, including sending emails, shopping and booking travel.

Meta said that Muse will now support voice and real-time video, enabling users have conversations. “Muse will work in the background and get things done for you as you're talking,” said Mark Zuckerberg, CEO of Meta in a post on X.

Meta also used Connect to expand its AI glasses lineup, introducing the Ray-Ban Meta Audio, its first camera-free smart glasses, alongside the third-generation Ray-Ban Meta.

The Audio glasses start at $349 and offer up to 12 hours of battery life, while the Gen 3 models start at $449 and add a 12MP camera, 3K video recording, up to nine hours of battery life and a six-microphone array. Meta said Muse will be available across its AI glasses, allowing users to access the agent hands-free.

The company also expanded its AI glasses portfolio with new Meta Glasses styles and said it expects to offer more than 100 glasses options across Ray-Ban, Oakley and Meta Glasses by the end of 2026.

title: Tech Mahindra Partners With Verato to Strengthen Healthcare AI Data Foundations
content:
Tech Mahindra will integrate Verato’s identity data platform into US healthcare transformation programmes to unify patient and provider records.

Tech Mahindra has partnered with identity intelligence company Verato to integrate identity intelligence into its healthcare transformation programmes in the US, serving health systems, payers, pharmaceutical companies and medical-device makers.

Under the partnership announced on September 23, Tech Mahindra will integrate Verato MDM Cloud into its healthcare transformation engagements. The platform matches and unifies patient, provider and member records across disparate systems, creating a consolidated view of identities.

The integration will be part of Tech Mahindra’s broader work across cloud modernisation, enterprise integration and digital transformation for healthcare clients. The company previously partnered with KOGO AI to develop private AI solutions for enterprises, with healthcare among the sectors targeted. That work involved integrating AI systems with existing enterprise ecosystems and legacy infrastructure.

Fragmentation is also a problem in healthcare automation workflows. A report on UiPath’s healthcare revenue-cycle-management work highlighted how disconnected systems, claims and document-heavy processes can complicate automation.

Verato’s platform is intended to resolve duplicate and mismatched records across system silos and enrich them with additional data and contextual information. Organisations can then feed the data into the systems where they need it.

“Every AI model inherits the identity data beneath it,” Joaquim Neto, Chief Strategy Officer at Verato, said.

Ravinder Singh, Global Vertical Head, Healthcare and Life Science (HLS), Tech Mahindra, said the partnership would strengthen its healthcare transformation capabilities by adding trusted identity intelligence to those services.

The companies did not disclose the financial terms of the partnership or name specific customers adopting the combined offering.

title: OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs Urge UN To Set Global Safeguards For AI
content:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei have called for global AI safeguards, warning that poorly managed AI could pose risks to humanity.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei have urged the United Nations to establish safeguards for artificial intelligence, warning that the technology could become difficult to control as its capabilities expand.

Speaking at a UN Security Council meeting on AI, Altman warned humanity “could lose control of the future to AI,” while Amodei called poorly managed AI “a risk to humanity as a whole.” Both urged the need for safeguards, including common testing standards and measures to verify advanced AI capabilities.

The discussion at the UN comes as governments grapple with how to manage increasingly capable AI systems without slowing their potential benefits. Altman and Amodei both argued that AI should not become concentrated in the hands of a single company or country. Altman also highlighted the potential of AI to improve people’s lives, while warning about the risks of losing control over its development.

Amodei called for countries to agree on measures to prevent AI from being used to develop biological weapons. He also proposed ways to verify the capabilities of advanced AI models and establish common standards for testing them, including tests for potential misuse and loss of control.

“Worries about control of AI are not a reason to pause its further development or to constrain it with new global governance structure,’” said White House Science Adviser Michael Kratsios. “We want you, our allies and partners, to share in the benefits of this technology,” he added.

China also weighed in, with UN Ambassador Fu Cong saying countries should be able to choose AI technologies according to their needs. The US and China are also discussing a possible mechanism to notify each other about AI incidents that could affect national security.

The UK is pushing for greater coordination, with Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband saying AI will be a major focus when the UK leads the G20 next year, including efforts to establish common global standards for safe AI development.

The debate also extended to military applications. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that AI could increasingly influence battlefield decisions and called for human control over machines. Experts also raised concerns about autonomous weapons and accountability when AI is involved in decisions involving the use of force.

title: Meta Unveils New Palm-Sized AI Device With Muse Agent
content:
Charm has a roughly 2-inch OLED touchscreen, built-in 5G connectivity and speakers and microphones.

Meta has unveiled Muse Charm, a palm-sized AI device that gives users direct access to its Muse personal AI agent without opening a phone app.

The company announced the device at its Meta Connect event and said the device brings Muse’s “state-of-the-art real-time voice model” into a pocket-sized form factor and will have more details later this year.

According to a report from Bloomberg, Charm has a roughly 2-inch OLED touchscreen, built-in 5G connectivity and speakers and microphones.

It can be carried in a pocket, worn on a wrist strap or attached to a bag or keychain.

The device has front and rear cameras that are primarily intended to give Muse visual information for analysis and AI-assisted actions, rather than simply serving as conventional phone cameras.

The device runs a dedicated operating system and displays a virtual Muse character that users can customise, including its appearance, clothing and voice.

It can also play music and video and includes a USB-C charging port, although it does not support phone or video calls. Users will set up and synchronise the Charm through the Muse app on an iPhone or Android phone.

The device is slated to ship in December, although Meta has not announced a price.

Bloomberg also reported that the project began as a prototype and was developed in roughly nine months by Meta’s new design team, led by former Apple design executive Alan Dye, in coordination with the Muse team.

Internally, the prototype was reportedly called ‘Clawmagochi’, combining its Tamagotchi-like design with the team’s interest in the OpenClaw AI assistant.

The announcement comes as Meta expands Muse across its hardware portfolio. The company has said Muse will become the primary AI interface for its smart glasses, where it can handle tasks and interact with users through voice.

Muse is designed as a general-purpose personal AI agent that can carry out tasks on a user’s behalf, including sending emails, shopping and booking travel.

Meta said that Muse will now support voice and real-time video, enabling users have conversations. “Muse will work in the background and get things done for you as you're talking,” said Mark Zuckerberg, CEO of Meta in a post on X.

Meta also used Connect to expand its AI glasses lineup, introducing the Ray-Ban Meta Audio, its first camera-free smart glasses, alongside the third-generation Ray-Ban Meta.

The Audio glasses start at $349 and offer up to 12 hours of battery life, while the Gen 3 models start at $449 and add a 12MP camera, 3K video recording, up to nine hours of battery life and a six-microphone array. Meta said Muse will be available across its AI glasses, allowing users to access the agent hands-free.

The company also expanded its AI glasses portfolio with new Meta Glasses styles and said it expects to offer more than 100 glasses options across Ray-Ban, Oakley and Meta Glasses by the end of 2026.

title: India’s Data Centre Boom is Creating Jobs Beyond Technology Roles: Report
content:
Data centre-related job postings in India rose to 1.3% in August, with demand spanning software, engineering, management, sales, and project management roles.

India’s expanding data centre capacity is creating employment demand beyond traditional technology roles, with data centre-related positions accounting for 1.3% of job postings in August, up from 1.0% a year ago, according to a report by Indeed Hiring Lab, the economic research arm of job site Indeed.

AI adoption is driving demand for larger data centre infrastructure across India, creating jobs beyond software development. While software roles accounted for 28% of data centre postings in FY26, demand also spanned management, engineering, sales, and project management, reflecting the sector’s broader employment needs.

India’s data centre boom is creating new jobs across both technical and non-technical roles.

“Data centres are complex, large-scale operations that require workers across engineering, project management, business operations and actions. As investment matures, this broader employment impact is likely to become increasingly visible in the labour market,” Callam Pickering, Senior Economist, APAC at Indeed, said in a statement.

The broader Indian job market also showed signs of strengthening in August. Job postings on Indeed increased 0.2% during the month and were 7.4% higher than a year earlier, while remaining 85% above pre-pandemic levels. However, Indeed's data primarily captures formal-sector recruitment and is therefore not representative of India's entire labour market, where informal employment remains significant.

Recent hiring growth has also been concentrated outside technology. Job postings increased in almost 80% of occupations over the past three months, led by childcare at 27%, nursing at 23%, pharmacy at 20%, and physicians and surgeons at 17%. Dental roles and medical technicians also recorded strong growth, at 16% and 14%, respectively.

Technology hiring, meanwhile, has weakened in recent months. Postings for IT infrastructure, operations and support fell 20%, while software development declined 19%, data and analytics fell 14%, and IT systems and solutions declined 7.6%.

Despite the slowdown, technology-related postings remain above pre-pandemic levels, although the sector has been weaker than the broader national hiring trend.

title: [Exclusive] Govt Eyes ₹20,000 Cr Fund to Back India’s Frontier AI Race
content:
The NFAICF is being structured as a SEBI-regulated Category I Alternative Investment Fund.

The Indian government, under the IndiaAI Mission, is exploring a ₹15,000–20,000 crore anchor investment for a proposed National Frontier AI & Compute Fund (NFAICF), according to a proposal note reviewed by AIM.

The proposed fund aims to provide long-term risk capital to India’s frontier AI companies as well as finance GPU clusters, specialised data centres, and other infrastructure required to build and scale these models. The proposal is still under consultation, with the final size, structure, governance, and role of government capital yet to be decided.

The proposed fund was discussed in a closed-door meeting on ‘Financing India’s Frontier & Compute Ecosystem’ in Delhi on September 24.

The session was hosted by Mohammed Y Safirulla K, Director, IndiaAI Mission; Sudeep Shrivastava, COO, IndiaAI Mission; and Saurabh Vijay, Chief Executive Officer, IndiaAI Mission. The meeting was attended by several Indian AI startups and AI ecosystem stakeholders, including Vivek Raghavan of Sarvam AI, PeakXV MD Rajan Anandan, and S Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.

According to a study by research institute Epoch AI, training large frontier models could cost more than $1 billion per run by 2027. The government says costs at this level could put frontier AI development beyond the reach of existing Indian venture capital and grant-based funding.

While the IndiaAI Mission offers access to subsidised compute and funding for indigenous foundation models through its ₹10,372 crore outlay, the government notes that there is currently no dedicated domestic equity vehicle to back frontier AI development.

That’s where it is trying to position NFAICF. The proposed fund intends to address the financing gap with patient capital over long-horizon research, development, and commercialisation cycles.

The NFAICF is being structured as a SEBI-regulated Category I Alternative Investment Fund. The investment decisions will be made by an Investment Committee comprising experts in technology, investment, infrastructure, and finance.

The proposed fund could consider different investment instruments, including venture and growth equity, convertible instruments, infrastructure equity, fund-of-funds commitments, and direct co-investments, depending on the company or infrastructure project.

The first is providing long-term capital to foundation model builders, specialised AI systems, and other strategically important AI technologies. The second is financing GPU clusters, specialised data centre capacity, and other AI compute infrastructure, while accounting for rapidly changing hardware, utilisation, power requirements, and demand visibility.

The government is considering linking compute investments to actual demand from AI companies and research institutions through capacity commitments, utilisation arrangements, or pre-agreed commercial terms. It estimates that this can reduce the risk of stranded or underused infrastructure.

The stakeholders are also examining secondary-market mechanisms that could give investors an exit without forcing companies into premature outcomes, given the decade-long investment horizons in traditional deeptech companies.

The government is also considering a follow-on and co-investment capability so the fund can participate in later rounds alongside private investors when strategically important companies need more capital.

The proposal is now being tested with frontier AI companies, data centre operators, cloud providers, GPU providers, domestic VCs, private equity funds, pension and insurance investors, multilateral institutions, and policymakers. The final design remains subject to stakeholder feedback and further assessment.

title: Claude Discovers CRISPR-Like Enzyme System as Anthropic Expands Into Wet-Lab Biology
content:
The company says Claude identified a novel enzyme system in bacteriophages after analysing over 2,00,000 reverse transcriptases.

Claude AI has identified a previously uncharacterised enzyme system with DNA repeat patterns reminiscent of CRISPR, in an early demonstration of how AI agents could be used to search biological data and generate hypotheses for laboratory testing.

The system, which Anthropic has named array-associated reverse transcriptases (ART), was found in bacteriophages, the viruses that infect bacteria. While earlier research identified the reverse transcriptase at the centre of the system, Anthropic says Claude was the first to identify the combination of the enzyme, an adjacent accessory protein, and a long array of repeated DNA sequences.

The company announced the finding alongside the launch of a new life sciences research group and laboratory. The work is currently described in a preprint, and researchers are still trying to determine what ART actually does.

Anthropic said Claude was given an initial prompt to search a large database for unusual reverse transcriptases. Around 950 Claude agents then worked for about 21 hours, using roughly 210 million tokens. The agents identified more than 2,00,000 reverse transcriptases, generated about 3,500 candidate systems and narrowed these down to 20 candidates for deeper analysis.

One agent eventually noticed a tandem repeat pattern next to an unusual reverse transcriptase. It compared the sequence with known systems, searched the scientific literature and generated a report for human researchers to investigate.

Anthropic’s scientists subsequently tested the candidate in the laboratory. The ART system consists of three components: a reverse transcriptase, a neighbouring partner gene and an array of evenly spaced DNA repeats. The repeat structure resembles the arrays found in CRISPR systems, which contain sequences that help make CRISPR-based systems programmable.

Initial laboratory experiments found that the ART array is expressed as multiple short RNAs. However, Anthropic has not yet established the biological function of the system or demonstrated that it can be used as a gene-editing tool.

Feng Zhang, a CRISPR genome-editing pioneer and professor at MIT and the Broad Institute, reviewed the preprint and described the identification of RNA-repeat arrays associated with reverse transcriptases as intriguing and worthy of further investigation.

Anthropic said it established its biology laboratory in spring 2026. Its researchers use Claude to analyse large collections of DNA sequences, examine protein families, identify unusual genomic patterns and generate hypotheses. Human scientists then decide which candidates are worth testing and conduct the laboratory experiments.

The company said its current work is limited to BSL-1 and BSL-2 research and that the laboratory does not handle pathogens that can infect humans. The physical laboratory work is performed by human scientists, with Claude being used primarily for computational analysis, hypothesis generation and interpretation of experimental results.

title: Accenture Launches New Vertical to Streamline AI Data Centre Infra Projects
content:
The new business builds on a capital projects unit that Accenture said has grown four times over three years and addresses a $260 billion market.

Accenture has launched Accenture Construct, a new global business that helps project owners plan, deliver, and optimise large infrastructure and capital projects, from airports and power grids to data centres, rail networks, and advanced manufacturing facilities.

According to a study commissioned by Accenture, the total addressable market for integrated owner-side capital project services is $260 billion and is projected to grow 7.5% annually to $348 billion in 2030.

"Global demand for critical infrastructure capital programmes is accelerating at the same time as AI is fundamentally changing how projects are planned, delivered and operated," Julie Sweet, Chair and CEO of Accenture, said in a statement.

Accenture said its capital projects business has grown four times over three years across strategic advisory, engineering, project delivery, and technology services. The company said the launch strengthens its position to capture growth from three converging demand cycles: the AI infrastructure build-out of data centre construction, the global energy transition, and long-term infrastructure replacement.

The company said fragmented delivery models can leave project owners absorbing the costs between multiple advisors, consultants, contractors, and specialist firms—each responsible for different parts of a project.

Accenture Construct addresses this through a common project data foundation designed to create a single operational view across the delivery ecosystem. The company said its AI-enabled workflows can shift project delivery from reactive management to predictive decision-making.

Accenture said Accenture Construct serves private and public sector clients and is organised around five global lines of business: data centres; utilities and telecommunications; transportation and civic infrastructure; advanced manufacturing; and process industries.

The business brings together more than 5,000 practitioners across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and Asia Pacific.

As representative engagements, Accenture cited Vale, the global mining company, where it is helping transform delivery of a large-scale annual industrial capital portfolio through digital engineering, AI, and integrated execution.

"Capital projects haven't lacked expertise; they've lacked alignment on shared success outcomes. Owners assemble exceptional teams, but accountability is often dispersed across the delivery ecosystem," said Adam J Shaw, CEO of Accenture Construct.

Accenture said the new business is designed to provide earlier risk identification and greater certainty over cost, schedule, quality, and asset performance. The company said Accenture Construct will act as a single accountable partner from strategy through handover.

title: Sol Emerges From Stealth With $4 Mn Haul to Build AI Assistant for Email Management
content:
The startup says its assistant proactively identifies email commitments and automates the process of researching, documenting, and drafting replies.

Sol, an artificial intelligence startup founded by former CRED executives, has emerged from stealth with $4 million in funding. The company said the round included participation from General Catalyst, Nexus Venture Partners, DeVC, Peercheque, and CRED founder and the current Global Head of WhatsApp, Kunal Shah.

Sol is building an AI assistant for email management. It proactively identifies commitments and automates the process of researching, documenting, and drafting replies without waiting for a manual prompt.

"People whose work runs through email often have to repeat themselves: first in email, then again when they ask an AI tool to act," said Anish Karan, CEO of Sol, in a statement. "If I've already said I'll do something, there should be an AI that gets started on it."

According to the company, Sol finds commitments expressed in Gmail, such as agreeing to send an analysis, share a proposal, or set up a meeting. It then gathers relevant context and starts the work needed to fulfil those commitments, including research, document and presentation creation, and meeting coordination. Users retain final approval before anything is sent, scheduled or shared, the company said.

The company said Sol operates in its own computer environment, can use a browser, and draws on a library of more than 100 specialist skills to complete multi-step tasks. As per the company, it intends to let Sol move from an email commitment to a finished draft or scheduled action, with the user approving or editing the result at the end.

Sol said it is designed for people whose work runs through high volumes of email, including founders, executives, and professionals in sales, marketing, consulting, recruiting, and agencies. The company is initially offering access through a waitlist at hellosol.app, and said it plans to expand general access.

Sol was founded by Anish Karan, Prateek Srivastava, and Ranjith Nair. Karan earlier worked on product retention and monetisation in CRED. Srivastava worked as the engineering leader at the fintech company, while Nair led the design and execution for CRED’s core payments products.

Akarsh Shrivastava, Partner at General Catalyst, said the firm's decision to back Sol was shaped by the founding team. "Anish is a second-time founder and one of the sharpest product minds we've worked with, turning referrals into a top growth channel for eighteen months in a market where they rarely work," Shrivastava said.

Jishnu Bhattacharjee, Partner at Nexus Venture Partners, said the firm was drawn to the product's simplicity. "What got us excited about Sol is that Anish and team are building AI that just knows when to act and proactively does the right things," Bhattacharjee said.

The company said it plans to extend general access to its AI assistant soon.

title: Qualcomm Unveils New Snapdragon Chips With On-Device AI at the Core
content:
The chips can run AI models locally, with features including personalised AI agents, voice processing, advanced camera controls and support for 30-billion-parameter models.

Qualcomm has launched two new flagship smartphone processors, Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, as it pushes to make on-device AI more capable and personalised.

The new chips are designed to support AI agents that can understand user behaviour, distinguish between speakers and build local memory from device usage. Qualcomm said the chips can run small AI models of up to 200 million parameters through a new sensing hub, while the higher-end Extreme variant can run a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model locally. The launch comes as chipmakers increasingly focus on running AI workloads directly on smartphones rather than relying entirely on cloud infrastructure.

The capability puts Qualcomm alongside other chipmakers working to bring larger AI models to consumer devices. Apple, for instance, introduced a 20-billion-parameter MoE model as part of its third-generation foundation models at its Worldwide Developers Conference in June.

“AI will now require the device to do much more than just execute commands, and it’s going to be less about navigating apps, and it’s going to be about completing tasks for you,” Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon said in his keynote speech at the Snapdragon Summit.

Qualcomm is also targeting AI-powered personalisation through the new sensing hub. The company said it can run models with up to 200 million parameters, allowing smartphones to handle tasks such as speaker identification and local transcription without sending all the data to the cloud.

According to the company, the chips can run a complete voice-in, voice-out AI agent locally, using a user’s interactions to build memory and offer more personalised suggestions and task automation. This allows more AI processing to happen directly on the smartphone.

The processor brings pixel-level camera control, improved stabilisation and motion understanding. The Extreme version supports 8K recording at 60fps and 4K at 240fps, as well as Qualcomm’s APV codec. Both chips use AI to improve vocals and reduce background noise during calls, with Voice Bubble designed to isolate the user’s voice.

Motorola has already announced a smartphone using the new platform. The Motorola Signature 27 will run on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, with general availability expected later this year.

The launch is part of Qualcomm’s broader push to make smartphones a central platform for AI. The company has been working on more than 40 AI-focused devices, while the smartphone industry continues to explore how much AI processing it can shift from the cloud to devices themselves.

Anthropic has launched Claude Opus 5.5, which delivers performance comparable to Claude Fable 5.1 on most work while costing 40% less to run than Opus 5.

The model is available immediately across Anthropic’s platforms, as well as Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

Anthropic is also increasing five-hour usage limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise subscribers, and introducing a rate-limit reset that users can save and use when needed. It did not disclose the new limits.

“Opus 5.5 is particularly good at long and sprawling jobs like codebase-wide migrations and audits,” Anthropic said in a blog post.

In one example the company cited, an early tester used Opus 5.5 to complete a migration involving a 680,000-line codebase in less than a day. Another tester used it to audit and fix a 200,000-line codebase in under three hours, while Opus 5 took more than 20 hours and used 2.5 times as many tokens.

The company also reported improvements on software optimisation tasks. When asked to reduce load times across every page of a web application, Opus 5.5 succeeded in 39 of 40 attempts, while Opus 5 generally produced smaller improvements and, in some cases, changed application behaviour, the company revealed.

On Anthropic’s benchmark suite, Opus 5.5 leads its comparison set on agentic coding, knowledge work, and computer-use evaluations.

It scores ahead of Fable 5.1 and Opus 5 on Terminal-Bench for sandbox state verification, code quality-focused FrontierCode, and CursorBench evaluating IDE efficiency, and leads the GDPval-AA knowledge work evaluation. OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra remains ahead on Anthropic’s scientific-research benchmark and narrowly leads its business-workflow evaluation.

The company said Opus 5.5 can match GPT-6 Astra on Terminal-Bench at roughly two-fifths of the cost per task, while exceeding Astra on FrontierCode at around one-fifth of the cost. On CursorBench, it said Opus 5.5 outperforms GPT-5.6 Sol at about a third of the cost.

However, Anthropic acknowledged limitations in its evaluation methods. “Building evaluations that reliably catch every failure prior to deployment remains an unsolved problem,” the company said.

Opus 5.5 costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, down from $5 and $25 for Opus 5. Cache reads have fallen from $0.50 to $0.20 per million tokens. Anthropic also said the model generates output more than 30% faster than Opus 5.

The model includes an action-screening classifier, an auditable open-source sandbox, and code review designed to catch vulnerabilities before changes are merged.

Anthropic said Opus 5.5 is more resistant to prompt injection than Opus 5 across coding, tool use, computer use, and web browsing. Its automated behavioural audit, covering nearly 2,000 scenarios, found improvements across most measures of misaligned behaviour.

Anthropic said there was an 85% reduction in Opus 5.5 attempting to circumvent containment compared with Opus 5 and Claude Mythos 5.1, while noting that models can sometimes recognise when they are being evaluated.

Because of its capabilities in cybersecurity and biology, Opus 5.5 launches with safeguards similar to Fable 5.1. Most cybersecurity tasks will be routed to Opus 4.8, while vetted organisations can apply for access to biology research. Anthropic also plans to expand its Cyber Verification Program to Opus 5.5.

Opus 5.5 also includes Anthropic’s preserved-thinking safeguard, which prevents API users from modifying Claude’s previous context to extract its reasoning at scale. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 are scheduled to follow in the coming weeks.

The model is also being released at the same time as OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and Luna.

Opus 5.5 offers slightly higher benchmark performance than GPT-6 Sol, albeit at a significantly higher price.

On FrontierCode, Opus 5.5 scored 51.4% at $2.25/task, versus Sol’s 48.4% at $1.37. On AutomationBench, Opus 5.5 scored 34.4% at $0.86, versus Sol’s 33.2% at $0.27.

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna With 50% Lower API Prices
content:
OpenAI said improvements in inference and prompt caching let it reduce serving costs while maintaining stronger performance.

OpenAI has launched GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, two lower-cost models built on the same technical advances as its GPT-6 Astra flagship.

The AI giant has also cut the API prices for the new models by 50% compared with the promotional pricing of their predecessors, the GPT-5.6 Sol and Luna.

GPT-6 Sol is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, while GPT-6 Luna costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens.

The company said improvements to inference and prompt caching let it reduce serving costs while maintaining stronger performance across professional workflows, coding, computer use, and factuality.

GPT-6 Sol is positioned for complex coding and agentic workloads, while Luna is designed for higher-volume tasks where cost is a larger constraint. Both models support a 1.05-million-token context window and up to 128,000 output tokens through the API.

On AutomationBench, which tests AI agents on end-to-end business workflows across sales, marketing, finance, support, and HR, OpenAI said GPT-6 Sol outperformed Claude Opus 5 and Claude Fable 5.1 while costing substantially less per task.

On DeepSWE, a benchmark for long-horizon software-engineering tasks in real codebases, Sol performed close to Claude Fable 5 while costing about 80% less per task.

OpenAI also reported similar cost efficiencies on other benchmarks, including the OSWorld 2.0 computer use tests, FrontierCode, Agents’ Last Exam, and more.

OpenAI is also increasing the economics of long-running agents through improved prompt caching.

“We’ve improved prompt caching for GPT‑6 to deliver higher cache hit rates by default, helping agents reuse more context, respond faster, and benefit from discounts of 90% on cached input-token reads,” said the company.

GPT-6 Sol and Luna are available through the API as gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna, and are being rolled out in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users. Free and Go users can access Luna through the desktop app. OpenAI is rolling out the models gradually in ChatGPT.

The launch comes shortly after OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Astra, leaving the company with a three-model GPT-6 family spanning its highest-capability model and lower-cost models intended for broader agentic and high-volume workloads.

However, these models are also being released at the same time as Anthropic's Claude 5.5 Opus. Opus 5.5 offers slightly higher benchmark performance than GPT-6 Sol, albeit at a significantly higher price.

On FrontierCode, Opus 5.5 scored 51.4% at $2.25/task, versus Sol’s 48.4% at $1.37. On AutomationBench, Opus 5.5 scored 34.4% at $0.86, versus Sol’s 33.2% at $0.27.

title: Navana.ai Launches Bodhi TTS at 60% Lower Price Than Sarvam
content:
Bodhi TTS offers sub-100ms response times, instant voice cloning and fine-grained pronunciation control for enterprise voice applications.

Navana.ai has launched Bodhi TTS, a text-to-speech model for Indian voice AI applications, with support for 10 Indian languages and more than 50 Indian voices.

The model is priced at ₹12 per 10,000 characters, which the company says is about one-eighth the price of ElevenLabs and 60% lower than Sarvam AI’s Bulbul v3.

Bodhi TTS supports Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi, Bengali, Odia, Malayalam, Kannada, English and Gujarati. Navana.ai said the model begins generating audio in under 100 milliseconds and can run inside an enterprise’s own data centre.

The company said Bodhi TTS is built and trained in India, with Navana.ai owning the speech stack end-to-end. It is designed to keep customer audio, transcripts and personal data within an enterprise’s security environment, without routing information through a third-party model provider.

At ₹12 per 10,000 characters, Bodhi TTS is priced below competing services. ElevenLabs lists its Multilingual and v3 models at $0.10 per 1,000 characters, which is about ₹95 per 10,000 characters, while Sarvam AI lists Bulbul v3 at ₹30 per 10,000 characters, according to Navana.ai.

“India runs on voice, and most of it is not in English. Until now, a bank that wanted a voice agent in Marathi or Tamil had to choose between a global model that mispronounced everyday words and a price that only worked for a pilot,” said Raoul Nanavati, Co-Founder and CEO of Navana.ai.

“We built Bodhi from the ground up to work to represent every accent, so in a country where every region speaks a little differently, businesses get fine-grained control from day one to make their bots sound truly Indian. And we priced it for the call volumes Indian businesses actually run, with everything in the box. One price, every voice, every feature,” he added.

Bodhi TTS is built to handle Indian-specific text formats. Navana.ai said it can read ₹1,00,000 as “one lakh rupees” and correctly vocalise PAN numbers, phone numbers, dates, EMIs, scheme names and account numbers.

The model also supports pronunciation control through dictionaries. Enterprises can upload product names, branch names and customer names, while a language model can mark up specific names inline for Bodhi TTS to pronounce according to the supplied instructions. Navana.ai said pronunciation issues identified during a live call can be corrected without retraining the model.

The company said its 50-plus voices are tuned for conversational phone interactions. New voices can be created from a few seconds of reference audio without additional training. Voice cloning is available across all 10 languages, with reference audio cached so that custom voices do not add latency during calls.

“Everyone assumes quality in speech scales with model size. For Indian speech it does not,” said Jai Nanavati, Co-Founder of Navana.ai.

“We built Bodhi TTS about five times smaller than the nearest comparable model. A small, fast model is one a bank can run on a mid-tier GPU it already owns, inside its own data centre. That is why we can price Bodhi the way we have, and why no customer data ever has to leave the building,” he added.

Navana.ai said its voice agents currently support more than ₹1,000 crore in monthly loan disbursals across its banking and lending customers. The company has processed more than 100 million voice AI minutes for BFSI customers, including Bajaj Finserv, Protean, Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, Jana Small Finance Bank and Grihum Housing Finance.

Alongside Bodhi TTS, Navana.ai has opened Bodhi STT, its speech recognition model supporting 10 Indian languages and more than 40 dialects, to customers by invitation. The company said benchmark results for the model have been published on Hugging Face.

Bodhi TTS is available through Navana.ai’s platform, with ₹1,000 in free credits for new users. Banks, insurers and lenders can also apply for early access to both Bodhi TTS and Bodhi STT. The first 100 approved teams will receive 100 hours of usage credits valid for 90 days.

title: Microsoft Offers Copilot Discounts of Up to 50% as It Prepares AI Super App: Report
content:
The reported discounts target large enterprise customers as Microsoft shifts Copilot toward usage-based billing and prepares a unified application for coding and AI agents.

Microsoft is offering discounts of up to 50% on its Copilot artificial intelligence software for large corporate customers, The Information reported. The discounts are tied to large seat commitments and additional usage-based payments for certain features, as Microsoft prepares to consolidate its Copilot experiences into a single application.

Microsoft is reportedly authorising discounts ranging from 30–50% for corporate customers that commit to large numbers of Copilot seats and additional usage-based payments. The discounts could begin as soon as October, according to a person with direct knowledge of the change cited by the publication.

The report said the discount could reach roughly 30% for customers with more than 1,000 Copilot seats, rising to 50% for customers with more than 10,000 seats. The reported discounts apply to Copilot subscriptions rather than representing a universal reduction in Microsoft’s standard pricing.

Shay Boloor, an analyst at The Futurum Group, also highlighted the development in a post on X that Microsoft was cutting Copilot pricing by about 40% for large enterprise customers while preparing a new Copilot ‘super app’ combining coding tools and AI agents.

Microsoft has separately confirmed plans to consolidate its Copilot experiences. During Microsoft’s fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter earnings call, Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella said Copilot’s chat, Cowork, Autopilot and Code experiences would come together in one ‘super app’ spanning consumer and commercial users.

“This is a major step forward,” Nadella said, adding that Microsoft would share more details.

Microsoft said Copilot had more than 30 million paid Microsoft 365 seats at the end of its fiscal fourth quarter. The company also reported that conversations per user had nearly doubled year over year and that average weekly engagement was on par with Outlook and Teams.

The reported pricing changes come as Microsoft moves Copilot beyond a purely per-seat licensing model. During the earnings call, Nadella described the company’s model as “seat plus usage”, while Microsoft said it was evolving its business model beyond per-seat licensing.

Microsoft has announced that usage-based billing will become the default for new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business licenses purchased through its Cloud Solution Provider channel starting November 2.

The model covers eligible usage-based experiences including Copilot Cowork, Work IQ APIs and GitHub Copilot Harness. Microsoft said pay-as-you-go will be the default billing configuration for the new CSP purchases.

Microsoft is reportedly pursuing the discounts as it expands Copilot’s seat-based business with usage-based revenue from newer AI features.

title: Meta Tests Human Contractors to Handle Calls for Muse AI Agent: Report
content:
Meta rolled back a test that used human contractors to handle some calls placed through its personal AI agent Muse after facing internal criticism over privacy and disclosure concerns.

Meta has been testing human contractors to handle some phone calls placed through its personal AI agent Muse, according to a Reuters report published September 22. The test involved contractors quietly handling calls placed through Muse, according to internal company posts Reuters accessed.

Muse is designed to perform tasks such as sending emails, shopping and booking travel. Its phone-calling feature lets users ask the agent to contact US businesses to book appointments, check whether products are in stock or obtain contractor quotes.

The human-contractor test came shortly after Meta launched the calling feature. Internal posts also showed that some users had encountered problems with AI-generated calls, including one case in which an insurance company ended a call after recognising the AI system.

Meta enabled the human-concierge feature for half of its employees last week, according to an internal post cited by Reuters. Under the test, Muse could hand a request to a trained human agent, who would place and handle the call. Employees who did not want to participate could opt out.

Some Meta employees raised concerns that human agents could be exposed to sensitive information during calls. Internal posts cited by Reuters showed employees warning that information could potentially be shared unintentionally with contractors working in call centres.

One employee also reported that a human contractor made a racist reference during a call with an internet and cable provider. Meta’s vice president in its Superintelligence Labs acknowledged that starting contractor-placed calls without proper disclosures was a mistake and said the company had “rolled back this feature” for now.

The executive also said some tests showed human-handled calls achieving success rates of 95% to 98%, compared with lower success rates for AI calling.

Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts said the company was working with merchants to improve the potential calling feature and would roll it out when it was ready and with the proper disclosures.

Muse has recorded more than 2.5 million downloads since its release, according to Sensor Tower data cited by Reuters. Meta has also highlighted security measures for the agent, including dedicated secure virtual machines and separate storage for sensitive information such as passwords.

title: MeitY Shortlists CoRover, Kyndryl for Agentic AI Platform: Report
content:
MeitY has shortlisted CoRover and Kyndryl Solutions to develop a reusable agentic AI platform for government services, with DigiLocker set to become its first use case.

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has reportedly narrowed the race to build its proposed agentic AI platform to CoRover and Kyndryl Solutions, with the government planning to test the technology first through DigiLocker.

According to Moneycontrol, MeitY plans to first implement the agentic platform on DigiLocker. The agent is expected to help users find and share documents, manage their digital document records, and retrieve information, subject to authentication and user consent.

The AI agent will be designed as a reusable “ask, do and escalate” framework that can answer citizen queries, carry out transactions, and hand off complex issues for human intervention.

Other than CoRover and Kyndryl Solutions, TCS, NEC Corporation, Cactus Technology Solutions, and Innefy Labs bid for technical evaluation for MeitY’s proposed agentic AI platform under the National e-Governance Division (NeGD).

“This initiative is part of NeGD’s broader effort to create sustainable institutional capacity for AI within government by creating a dedicated team which will address AI-specific problem statements across domains such as citizen services, analytics, process optimisation, and automation,” the tender for technical evaluation issued on August 10 read.

The DigiLocker implementation is planned over four months, followed by 12 months of operations and maintenance. MeitY’s larger plan is to build the underlying technology as a reusable framework, so that similar agents can be deployed across other government services without developing a separate system from scratch.

The architecture is expected to support Parichay and DigiLocker authentication, consent management, and audit trails. It will also support multiple Indian languages and different deployment models, including SaaS APIs and on-premises infrastructure.

title: India’s GCCs Face AI Shift as Nearly 70% Remain Stuck at Pilot Stage: Report
content:
By 2030, Indian GCCs are reportedly set to become engines of agentic transformation.

Indian GCCs are moving towards a more strategic role in enterprise AI, but nearly 70% remain stuck at the pilot stage due to gaps in data, infrastructure, governance and talent, according to a new report by Dell Technologies and Zinnov.

India currently has more than 2,100 GCCs employing 2.36 million people and generating $98.4 billion in revenue in FY26. The report found that 70% of GCCs have a defined AI roadmap or charter, while more than 1,200 centres have already built AI and machine learning capabilities. Indian GCCs account for around 28% of global GCC AI talent.

However, the report said the rapid adoption of AI is exposing structural gaps within these centres. Fragmented data, legacy systems, unclear governance, immature security controls and workforce models designed for pre-AI operations are preventing many AI proofs of concept from reaching production.

The economics of moving from pilots to production are also changing with the rise of agentic AI. According to the report, agentic workflows can consume between 10,000 and 500,000 tokens per workflow, compared with 1,000 to 2,000 tokens for a standard chat interaction. This makes decisions around compute, infrastructure, tooling and workload architecture increasingly important for GCCs.

The report identifies four areas that could reshape the GCC operating model: embedding AI into core business functions, planning infrastructure and architecture ahead of production, taking ownership of products and markets, and redesigning roles as AI automates repetitive work.

Workforce transformation is expected to be another major pressure point. Around 55% of routine GCC work is exposed to AI-driven automation, while 60% of the workforce will require reskilling by 2030, according to the report. It argues that GCCs will need to move beyond incremental AI training towards broader changes in roles and responsibilities.

The report also recommends that GCCs make infrastructure decisions based on the nature of individual AI workloads. Sensitive data, regulatory requirements, business-critical processes and predictable high-volume workloads may require greater infrastructure control, while lower-risk or exploratory workloads could be handled through leased or managed environments.

“The most influential GCCs of 2030 will not be measured by the number of AI initiatives they launch, but by their ability to industrialise AI responsibly and at scale,” said Manish Gupta, President and Managing Director, Dell Technologies India.

Dell Technologies and Zinnov have also proposed a ‘Sovereign Sandbox’ model for GCCs experimenting with regulated or proprietary data. The model is intended to provide a controlled environment for experimentation before workloads move into production.

“The next decade will be about ownership. As AI and agentic systems become embedded into enterprise workflows, GCCs will increasingly be expected to own products, platforms, markets, and measurable business outcomes,” said Sidhant Rastogi, President, Zinnov.

The report also noted that the GCC maturity cycle is shortening, with 27% of new GCCs reaching Portfolio Hub maturity within five years, compared with nearly a decade historically.

title: SpaceXAI Launches Grok 4.7 for Coding, Long-Horizon Agentic Knowledge Work
content:
On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Grok 4.7 ranks fourth, only behind Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Claude Opus 5.

SpaceXAI has launched Grok 4.7, its latest AI model focused on coding and professional knowledge work, claiming improvements in speed, reasoning, and handling complex tasks.

Grok 4.7 uses a larger base model and longer reinforcement-learning training to improve its ability to work on tasks that take hours to complete. According to xAI, the model performs better at checking its own work, creating documents and presentations, and handling cybersecurity tasks.

It is available through Grok Build, Cursor, and the Grok API, starting at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens.

SpaceXAI said Grok 4.7 is designed for coding and professional knowledge work. It uses a larger base model than Grok 4.6. The model underwent a longer reinforcement-learning training process focused on more difficult tasks, particularly those that can take several hours to complete.

“Grok 4.7 is a strong combination of intelligence, speed, and low cost,” Elon Musk, Founder of SpaceXAI (formerly xAI), stated on X.

The company claims, for biological safety, Grok 4.7 scored 62.4% on LatchBio’s biosafety benchmark.

On the AA Briefcase benchmark, which evaluates long-horizon agentic work, Grok 4.7 scored 1,657, compared with 1,546 for Grok 4.6. On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, which evaluates end-to-end software engineering performance, it ranks fourth, only behind Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Claude Opus 5.

The model comes with a new safeguard system focused on cybersecurity and other dual-use areas. Grok 4.7 demonstrated stronger resistance to jailbreak attempts while maintaining its ability to assist with legitimate security work, according to the company. It reported that 3.3% of risky dual-use prompts were allowed through on its HackerBench v0.3 evaluation.

The company has also begun providing selected cybersecurity partners with invite-only access to the model’s red-team capabilities for defensive research.

title: OpenAI’s Model Cracks 100+ Maths Problems, Surprises Its Own Mathematicians
content:
The company is now establishing an independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence, hosted at the Institute for Advanced Study.

OpenAI said an internal AI model that recently produced a proposed solution to the 90-year-old Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem has now resolved more than 100 long-standing open problems across most areas of mathematics.

“The pace of its progress⁠ in mathematics has surprised the mathematicians within OpenAI,” said the company in a blog post.

Thus, OpenAI is now establishing an independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence, hosted at the Institute for Advanced Study.

The nine-member group will advise on reviewing emerging results, communicating their significance, coordinating their dissemination and applying academic and professional standards to AI-generated mathematical research.

The announcement comes shortly after mathematicians published an open letter, ‘A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics’, raising concerns about the use of solving open mathematical problems as a benchmark for AI systems.

The letter argues that rapid AI progress could create negative externalities for the mathematical research community.

The declaration, published by 25 Fields Medal winners, including Terence Tao, Peter Scholze and Cédric Villani, argues that AI companies’ focus on solving mathematical problems as benchmarks risks prioritising answers over the understanding and ideas that mathematics is intended to develop.

The mathematicians said AI-generated results can also arrive too quickly for the community to properly explain, simplify and connect them to previous work, raising concerns around attribution and plagiarism.

They argued that AI could accelerate mathematical research, but said its impact would depend on whether researchers preserve the human processes through which new ideas are understood, discussed and incorporated into the field.

Therefore, this group will advise on how AI tools can support mathematical research and learning. OpenAI said it wants mathematicians to use increasingly capable AI systems to pursue research questions and develop new ideas.

“We want to put capable tools in mathematicians’ hands so they can pursue the questions they know best and develop new ideas,” OpenAI said.

The initial group includes mathematicians François Charles, Camillo De Lellis, Timothy Gowers, Martin Hairer, Nikhil Srivastava, Ulrike Tillmann, Ravi Vakil, Edward Witten and Melanie Matchett Wood.

OpenAI said the group would operate independently, with members free to exercise their own judgement, challenge the company and publish advice publicly.

Its members will not be paid by OpenAI, will control the group’s membership, and will not have a role in setting the pace of OpenAI’s internal mathematics research.

title: Matters.AI, Cockroach Labs Launch Data Security Integration for DPDP-Regulated Data
content:
The integration maps sensitive data in CockroachDB to the users, roles and privileges that can access it, while keeping raw data within the customer’s infrastructure.

Bengaluru-based AI-native data security company Matters.AI and Cockroach Labs, the company behind the distributed SQL database CockroachDB, have launched an integration to identify personal and regulated data within CockroachDB deployments and map it to the database users, roles and privileges that can access it.

The integration, available to CockroachDB customers, classifies data at the column level and creates an access map showing which accounts can reach regulated data, where excessive privileges exist and whether data is stored in a jurisdiction where it should not be.

The launch comes as Indian enterprises prepare for compliance with the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules. The rules were notified in November 2025, with substantive obligations for data fiduciaries scheduled to take effect from May 2027. Banks, payment companies and insurers are also subject to existing data-localisation and cybersecurity requirements from the Reserve Bank of India.

According to the companies, the integration scans CockroachDB databases, tables and columns using 38 personally identifiable information (PII) detectors covering eight regulatory jurisdictions. It can also detect payment card numbers, protected health information and secrets stored in free-text columns.

The classified data is then correlated with CockroachDB users, roles and privilege grants. This allows security teams to identify which accounts can access regulated information, which roles have privileges beyond their current usage and where regulated data may be located outside the appropriate jurisdiction. The findings can be mapped against requirements under the DPDP Act, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO 27001 and SOC 2.

A key feature of the integration is that data classification and privilege analysis take place inside the customer’s own infrastructure. The companies said raw records and sampled values are not transmitted to the Matters.AI control plane; only findings and operational metadata are sent.

For Indian organisations subject to data-residency requirements, the companies said this architecture allows security analysis without moving the underlying customer data outside the organisation’s environment.

“Enterprises distributed their databases to survive anything. In doing so, they made their most sensitive data harder to see than ever: more regions, more tables, more roles, and still no answer to the simplest question a CISO can ask: who can reach this data right now?” said Keshava Murthy, Co-Founder and CEO of Matters.AI. He added that the integration provides this visibility at the column level within the customer's own environment.

The companies cited IBM’s Cost of a Data Breach Report 2026, which puts the average cost of a data breach in India at ₹25.5 crore, up 15.9% year on year. The report puts the average cost for financial services organisations at ₹40.9 crore per breach. Indian organisations without security automation took an average of 236 days to identify a breach, according to the release.

The release also points to penalties under the DPDP Act, with the Data Protection Board of India able to impose penalties of up to ₹250 crore per instance for failure to implement reasonable security safeguards.

“Together with Matters.AI, we’re making data protection seamless for our customers. This integration gives teams instant visibility into where their sensitive data lives, who can access it, and what's happening to it,” said Tejas Baldev, Vice President of Sales, APAC, at Cockroach Labs.

title: Google Hit With $440 Mn Penalty for Breaching EU Privacy Rules Over Location Data
content:
Ireland’s data protection regulator fined Google for violating EU privacy rules over how it processed users’ location data between 2018 and 2020.

In 2023, it fined Meta a whopping €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion) for transferring EU user data to the US. A year earlier, it had fined Instagram for violations concerning the processing of children’s personal data.Ireland’s Data Protection Commission (DPC) has fined Google €403 million ($440 million) for breaching EU privacy rules when it comes to processing users’ location data, in one of the regulator’s largest penalties against a major technology company.

According to the DPC findings, Google had violated the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) through three features—Web & App Activity, Location History, and Location Accuracy—between 2018 and 2020. The regulator said users may not have been adequately aware that their location data could be used to influence advertising or infer their interests.

It identified transparency violations across the three features. The regulator further found that Google retained certain location data through Web & App Activity and Location History for longer than was necessary.

The DPC’s investigation was conducted under the GDPR’s one-stop-shop mechanism, under which a lead supervisory authority can oversee cross-border processing by companies operating across multiple EU countries. Ireland has become the lead data protection regulator for several major US technology companies because many of them have their European headquarters or main EU operations in Ireland.

"As a result of Google’s failures, individuals could have been unaware that their location was being used to, for example, influence them with ads or to infer their interests, and could lose control over their personal data," DPC Deputy Commissioner and Head of Communications Graham Doyle stated.

Alongside the financial penalty, the DPC has ordered Google to bring its processing of location data into compliance with the GDPR within six months.

In response to the penalty, Google stated that it has introduced new controls to manage location data and advertising preferences, following concerns over its historical policies. It now allows users to automatically delete personal data on a rolling basis, store timeline ⁠data directly ​on a device, and manage how data, including location, is ​used for ads.

The €403 million penalty makes it the fourth-largest fine imposed by Ireland’s DPC since the regulator became the lead supervisory authority for many major technology companies under the GDPR.

The company is now establishing an independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence, hosted at the Institute for Advanced Study.

OpenAI said an internal AI model that recently produced a proposed solution to the 90-year-old Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem has now resolved more than 100 long-standing open problems across most areas of mathematics.

“The pace of its progress⁠ in mathematics has surprised the mathematicians within OpenAI,” said the company in a blog post.

Thus, OpenAI is now establishing an independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence, hosted at the Institute for Advanced Study.

The nine-member group will advise on reviewing emerging results, communicating their significance, coordinating their dissemination and applying academic and professional standards to AI-generated mathematical research.

The announcement comes shortly after mathematicians published an open letter, ‘A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics’, raising concerns about the use of solving open mathematical problems as a benchmark for AI systems.

The letter argues that rapid AI progress could create negative externalities for the mathematical research community.

The declaration, published by 25 Fields Medal winners, including Terence Tao, Peter Scholze and Cédric Villani, argues that AI companies’ focus on solving mathematical problems as benchmarks risks prioritising answers over the understanding and ideas that mathematics is intended to develop.

The mathematicians said AI-generated results can also arrive too quickly for the community to properly explain, simplify and connect them to previous work, raising concerns around attribution and plagiarism.

They argued that AI could accelerate mathematical research, but said its impact would depend on whether researchers preserve the human processes through which new ideas are understood, discussed and incorporated into the field.

Therefore, this group will advise on how AI tools can support mathematical research and learning. OpenAI said it wants mathematicians to use increasingly capable AI systems to pursue research questions and develop new ideas.

“We want to put capable tools in mathematicians’ hands so they can pursue the questions they know best and develop new ideas,” OpenAI said.

The initial group includes mathematicians François Charles, Camillo De Lellis, Timothy Gowers, Martin Hairer, Nikhil Srivastava, Ulrike Tillmann, Ravi Vakil, Edward Witten and Melanie Matchett Wood.

OpenAI said the group would operate independently, with members free to exercise their own judgement, challenge the company and publish advice publicly.

Its members will not be paid by OpenAI, will control the group’s membership, and will not have a role in setting the pace of OpenAI’s internal mathematics research.

title: Delvitech to Invest Up to $30 Mn in Bengaluru Manufacturing Facility, Create 800 Jobs
content:
The 65,000-square-foot facility is expected to become operational in Q1 2027 and is projected to create 500–800 jobs over the next five years

Swiss electronics inspection technology company Delvitech will invest an initial $10 million, with total investment expected to reach $25–30 million, to establish a new manufacturing and technology facility in Bengaluru as it expands its presence in India’s growing electronics manufacturing ecosystem.

The 65,000-square-foot facility is expected to become operational in Q1 2027 and is projected to create 500–800 jobs over the next five years, spanning manufacturing, engineering and technical roles.

The company, which develops AI-native Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) solutions for electronics manufacturing, announced the investment on September 22, alongside a showcase of its latest inspection technologies at productronica India 2026 in Bengaluru.

“India is one of our priority markets, and the country has leapfrogged in its manufacturing capabilities over the last few years, with electronics now being at the center of that growth story. We see enormous potential here; not just as a manufacturing base, but increasingly as a hub for R&D and innovation. Our customers here didn’t ask us to be present; they asked us to be close. Bangalore is that answer,” Roberto Gatti, Founder and CEO of Delvitech SA, said.

The Bengaluru facility will bring precision machining, metrology and equipment integration under one roof, with Delvitech aiming to localise engineering support and improve control over manufacturing quality and lead times.

“The new facility brings together in-house precision machining, metrology and equipment integration under one roof, allowing us to control quality and tolerances at every stage, shorten lead times, and localise engineering support for our customers. We are investing in India for the long term, building a facility that goes beyond assembly to deliver real manufacturing, technology and customer value locally,” Vasanth Kumar, Head of Asia Operations, Delvitech, said.

The facility will include an in-house Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) and metrology equipment to inspect critical components for accuracy, repeatability and compliance. It will also integrate mechanical, electrical, optical, software and control systems, supported by engineering and R&D teams focused on localisation and continuous improvement. Delvitech also plans to establish a dedicated customer demonstration area, allowing customers to locally test and evaluate its inspection machines.

Alongside the facility announcement, Delvitech showcased its latest inspection solutions—including Horus, Aton and Horus Dual Lane—at productronica India 2026.

The company said its systems use physical AI to transform electronics inspection, focusing on improving manufacturing efficiency, cost, production time and sustainability.

Delvitech is betting on rising demand for automated inspection as Indian original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and electronics manufacturing services (EMS) companies scale production and adopt higher levels of automation and traceability.

The Bengaluru facility is expected to bring Delvitech’s manufacturing, engineering, inspection technology and customer support capabilities closer to Indian electronics manufacturers as the country expands its role in global electronics production.

title: Delinea Joins Anthropic’s Project Glasswing to Use AI Against Its Own Security Code
content:
The initiative will apply AI-driven defensive cybersecurity techniques to Delinea’s own systems.

Identity security company Delinea has joined Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, using Anthropic’s frontier AI model Claude Mythos 5.1 to test and identify vulnerabilities in its own software, including code responsible for credential vaulting, secrets management and privileged session brokering.

The initiative will apply AI-driven defensive cybersecurity techniques to Delinea’s own systems, with the company focusing on code paths where vulnerabilities could expose privileged access across the systems it governs.

“AI is making it much easier to find weaknesses in software, and that changes what customers should expect from security companies,” said Art Gilliland, CEO at Delinea. “We joined Project Glasswing to use the best tools available to attack our own assumptions and find problems before someone else does.”

As part of Project Glasswing, Delinea will use Mythos to examine several security-critical areas of its software. These include credential and secrets handling, covering vaulting logic, secret storage and rotation, key management and cryptographic implementations. The model will also examine session brokering and privileged access paths, including the connection, injection and proxy code that sits between users or AI agents and target systems.

The assessment will also cover authorisation enforcement, including policy evaluation and just-in-time authorisation paths, where flaws in access-control logic can potentially be as consequential as memory-safety vulnerabilities. Findings from the AI-led testing will be fed into

Delinea’s existing software development lifecycle, where they will be triaged and remediated. The company said it could then incorporate recurring vulnerability patterns into secure coding standards, pre-merge checks and test coverage.

Project Glasswing brings together organisations whose software supports critical infrastructure and where successful attacks could have significant consequences. Delinea said identity security belongs in this category because vulnerabilities in identity systems could potentially expose the systems and resources they govern access to.

Delinea said it will treat the AI model’s access to its code as a privileged identity, with access scoped, temporary and logged. Mythos will operate in an isolated environment, with no customer data included in its scope.

“We’re treating Mythos like any other privileged identity: its access is scoped, temporary and logged,” said Pierre Mouallem, Chief Information Security Officer at Delinea. “It runs against our code in an isolated environment with no customer data in scope. Anything it finds enters the same product security and disclosure process as a human-reported vulnerability.”

Delinea said validated findings and remediation patterns will be shared with the Project Glasswing cohort. For vulnerabilities affecting third-party or open-source components, the company will follow coordinated vulnerability disclosure timelines. Vulnerabilities affecting Delinea products will be disclosed through the company’s Security Advisories process.

The partnership comes as AI-assisted vulnerability discovery becomes increasingly relevant to cybersecurity, potentially allowing both attackers and defenders to identify software weaknesses faster and at greater scale.

For Delinea, the Glasswing initiative aims to use those capabilities defensively by applying them directly to the code underpinning privileged identity and access controls.

title: CoRover.ai Partners With Tech Mahindra to Take India-Built AI to Global Markets
content:
CoRover.ai and Tech Mahindra will combine their AI platforms to develop sovereign, enterprise, and agentic AI solutions for customers in India and global markets.

CoRover.ai has partnered with Tech Mahindra to develop and deploy AI solutions for enterprises, governments, and public institutions, with the collaboration centred on sovereign AI, enterprise AI, agentic AI, and digital public infrastructure.

The partnership will combine CoRover’s BharatGPT platform with Tech Mahindra’s Project Indus and TechM Orion platforms. The companies will build AI solutions that account for local language, context, operational requirements, and data sovereignty, while adapting them for use across international markets.

They will also explore applications across public institutions, citizen services, and enterprise transformation.

“This partnership gives us an opportunity to combine our AI platforms with Tech Mahindra’s technology, engineering depth, and execution capabilities,” Ankush Sabharwal, Co-founder and CEO, CoRover.ai, said in a statement.

Tech Mahindra said the partnership will build on AI initiatives developed in India and extend them across industries and geographies.

“India has demonstrated its ability to create meaningful AI innovation. The next opportunity is to translate that innovation into solutions that can be adopted at scale by enterprises, governments, and institutions,” said Nikhil Malhotra, Chief AI and Innovation Officer, Tech Mahindra.

“Through this partnership, we are bringing together indigenous AI platforms, engineering expertise, and global market reach to create capabilities that are rooted in local context while addressing opportunities across international markets,” Malhotra added.

The partnership comes as Indian technology companies and IT services providers expand efforts to develop AI systems that can be deployed according to the language, regulatory, and sovereignty requirements of different markets.
