Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has acquired two large land parcels in Visakhapatnam and Pune that are expected to house OpenAI’s first data centre facilities in India, according to a report by The Economic Times.

The Andhra Pradesh government has allotted 200 acres to TCS in Anakapalli district near Visakhapatnam, a region that is rapidly emerging as a hub for AI infrastructure. The site is located close to Google’s under-construction 1 GW hyperscale data centre, positioning the area as a key destination for large-scale AI and cloud investments.

Separately, TCS has purchased an 88-acre land parcel in Bopkhel, Pune, from Hemisphere Properties for ₹640.5 crore. The public sector enterprise is responsible for monetising assets formerly owned by Videsh Sanchar Nigam Limited (VSNL), now Tata Communications.

According to the report, the two sites are expected to support OpenAI’s infrastructure expansion in India as the company scales its computing capacity to serve growing demand for AI services.

The Visakhapatnam site adds to Andhra Pradesh’s efforts to attract hyperscale data centre investments, while the Pune acquisition strengthens TCS’ infrastructure footprint in one of India’s largest technology hubs. The report said both locations are being considered for OpenAI’s first data centre facilities in the country.

The development follows a broader trend of global AI companies expanding data centre capacity in India to meet rising demand for model training and inference workloads.

The country has also been positioning itself as a destination for AI infrastructure through state-backed compute initiatives and growing private sector investments.

The land acquisitions build on the strategic partnership announced by The Tata Group and OpenAI in February. Under the agreement, OpenAI became the first customer of TCS’ HyperVault data centre business, with an initial commitment of 100 MW of AI-ready capacity that could scale to 1 GW over time. The partnership is part of OpenAI’s global Stargate initiative to build AI infrastructure outside the US while supporting data residency, security and low-latency AI services in India.

Samsung has established a robotics division that reports directly to the CEO to enhance its robotics strategy and commercialisation efforts.

The new RX division will focus on developing humanoid robots for manufacturing, home, and retail applications.

Samsung Electronics has created a dedicated robotics division that will report directly to its CEO as the South Korean company steps up efforts to develop and commercialise robotics technologies, Reuters reported. It said the robots will first be deployed at manufacturing sites before expanding into home and retail applications.

The new RX, or Robotics eXperience, division will lead the company’s long-term robotics strategy, technology development and business execution as Samsung looks to make robotics a future growth engine. The company became the largest shareholder in Rainbow Robotics in late 2024 to accelerate humanoid robot development and has since increased its focus on physical AI and industrial automation.

It also appointed Executive Vice President Lee Dongkun to lead its Robotics Strategy Team. Lee previously led robotics strategy at Hyundai Motor Group, including overseeing the direction of Boston Dynamics. Samsung said it will also establish robotics research hubs in the United States, China and Japan to strengthen its capabilities by drawing on local expertise and innovation ecosystems.

According to a company statement cited by reports, the RX division will oversee Samsung’s mid- to long-term robotics strategy while expanding research capabilities in South Korea and overseas.

The planned research hubs will support technology development in regions where robotics innovation is advancing rapidly. Samsung said the move will help improve its competitiveness through collaboration with local ecosystems.

The announcement builds on Samsung’s broader push into robotics over the past year. During its January earnings conference call, the company said it expected to achieve “tangible” results in its humanoid robotics business this year.

Samsung’s announcement also comes as companies increase investments in humanoid robots for industrial use. Last week, Hyundai Motor Group said it would acquire SoftBank’s remaining stake in Boston Dynamics, giving it full ownership of the robotics company.

In April, Samsung said it was open to investments and acquisitions to accelerate robotics development and commercialisation. It also said it would work with local companies on technology development where required.

Samsung said advances in technologies such as physical AI are making robotics businesses increasingly viable. The company plans to develop humanoid robots to improve productivity and user experience.

The announcement reflects the growing convergence of AI and robotics, with companies increasingly combining foundation models and physical AI to develop humanoid robots. Samsung has said advances in physical AI are making robotics commercially viable.

content:
Indian clinicians exhibit higher trust in AI tools than their global counterparts, despite lower adoption rates.

Only 42% of Indian clinicians currently use AI, below the global average of 49%.

Indian clinicians trust artificial intelligence (AI) more than their global counterparts, but its adoption in clinical practice remains below the global average, according to Elsevier’s Clinician of the Future 2026 report.

The report found that 42% of clinicians in India currently use AI for work compared to the global average of 49%. Despite the lower adoption, 43% of Indian clinicians said they trust AI tools, higher than the global average of 37%.

Based on responses from 2,757 clinicians, including 2,065 doctors and 692 nurses across 118 countries, the report also found that Indian healthcare professionals reported better workplace conditions and greater institutional preparedness for AI than their global peers.

Around 53% of Indian respondents said their institutions have good AI governance, compared to 40% globally. Similarly, 50% rated their access to digital tools positively, while 44% said they receive adequate AI training, both higher than the global averages of 41% and 32%, respectively.

Indian clinicians also reported lower workplace pressure. Nearly 79% said they have sufficient time to provide quality patient care, compared to 65% globally. Only 12% said they were considering leaving their jobs, significantly lower than the global average of 24%.

Elsevier also found that AI is becoming increasingly common in healthcare worldwide. Nearly half of clinicians now use AI at work, with 56% of AI users regularly relying on general-purpose tools such as ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot. Meanwhile, 34% frequently use clinical-specific AI tools for tasks such as clinical decision-making, second opinions and patient care support.

The report noted that clinicians expect AI to become more deeply integrated into healthcare over the next decade. Around 80% believe AI will become a critical assistant in clinical decision-making within the next five to 10 years, while 58% said clinicians using AI are likely to deliver better-quality care than those who do not.

Despite growing confidence in AI, Elsevier highlighted the need for greater transparency around how AI models are trained and how they generate outputs. The report said clinicians need to trust these systems as they increasingly rely on them to support life-critical medical decisions.

Among the countries surveyed, Japan recorded the highest trust in AI at 54%, followed by China (49%), while the United States (19%) and the United Kingdom (21%) reported the lowest levels of trust.

Google is developing a new AI server chip, internally called Frozen v2, that is designed to run its Gemini models more efficiently by embedding parts of the models directly into the chip’s hardware, according to a report by The Information.

The chip is expected to process six to 10 times more AI tokens for the same amount of electricity than Google’s latest tensor processing units (TPUs), if internal targets are met.

Unlike Google’s general-purpose TPUs, Frozen v2 is being built specifically for inference, the stage where trained AI models generate responses. By hardwiring portions of Gemini’s neural network architecture into silicon, Google expects to reduce the amount of computation required to serve AI models while lowering power consumption. The chip is not intended to replace TPUs but to complement them for large-scale inference workloads.

The project comes as Google faces growing demand for AI compute across its own products and Google Cloud.

According to the report, shortages in AI computing capacity have forced the company to prioritise internal workloads and turn away some external cloud customers. Improving inference efficiency could allow Google to serve more AI requests without expanding data centre capacity at the same pace.

The report said Frozen v2 could enter production as early as 2028. The chip is expected to be used primarily for Google’s Gemini models, rather than supporting a broad range of AI workloads like existing TPUs.

Google has expanded its custom silicon efforts over the past decade to reduce reliance on third-party AI hardware. Its TPU lineup powers AI training and inference across Google services and Google Cloud, where the company also offers TPU access to external developers and enterprises.

IT services firm Cognizant has secured a multi-year technology services contract from US health insurer Centene Corp, in a deal valued at more than $500 million and potentially approaching $1 billion, according to a Moneycontrol report citing people familiar with the matter.

The report said the exact value of the engagement could vary depending on its final structure.

As Centene is an existing Cognizant customer, the contract is expected to comprise both renewal of existing work and new business.

According to the report, Cognizant is expected to deploy its TriZetto healthcare software platform alongside its recently launched agentic AI offerings, including Flowsource and Agent Foundry, to support functions such as medical claims processing, billing automation, and customer service operations.

AIM has reached out to Cognizant regarding the development but did not receive a response at the time of publishing.

Cognizant and Centene had entered into a $2.7 billion master services agreement in 2014 through Health Net, but the arrangement was restructured after Centene acquired Health Net in 2016. Centene is a Fortune 500 company that primarily acts as an intermediary for government sponsored health programmes, focusing on uninsured and low-income groups.

The reported deal comes as large IT services providers increasingly pitch AI-led transformation rather than traditional labour-arbitrage outsourcing, with enterprises restructuring long-term contracts into shorter, outcome-based engagements. In the January-March 2026 quarter, Cognizant reported a 21% year-over-year increase in bookings.

Cognizant is scheduled to report its second-quarter results on July 29, 2026. Its shares closed 0.29% lower on Nasdaq on July 20.

Accenture has appointed former McKinsey & Company partner Pradeep Prabhala as the lead of its India Market Unit, effective September 1, as the global consulting and technology services company doubles down on artificial intelligence-led transformation and India’s expanding GCC market.

Prabhala will lead Accenture’s India business, working with domestic clients on data and AI-led transformation initiatives while also supporting multinational companies setting up and expanding GCCs in the country, the company said in a statement on July 21.

The appointment comes as global consulting and IT services firms are increasingly repositioning their India operations beyond traditional outsourcing, focusing instead on AI deployment, digital transformation and GCC advisory services as enterprises ramp up technology investments.

Prabhala joins Accenture from McKinsey & Company, where he was a partner leading the firm’s consumer sector practice in India and agriculture practice across Asia.

Before that, he spent nearly a decade at Monitor Deloitte, advising companies on growth strategy, market expansion, mergers and acquisitions, and digital transformation.

In his new role, Prabhala will also help global clients build and scale GCCs, which have emerged as one of the fastest-growing segments of India’s technology and business services ecosystem, with multinational companies increasingly using them for engineering, AI, product development and innovation.

“India is a strategic market for Accenture, and we are focused on accelerating growth here. As clients deepen their focus on technology-led reinvention and unlocking new value from data and AI, we see tremendous opportunity to help them lead,” Arundhati Chakraborty, Global Lead, Finance and GCC and Executive Sponsor, India Market Unit, Accenture said in the statement.

Beyond his consulting career, Prabhala is an early-stage investor in AI, enterprise software and deep technology startups across India and the US.

The Telangana government has partnered with Microsoft, the 1M1B Foundation (One Million for One Billion), and MeitY Startup Hub to establish India’s first Green Skills and Applied AI Centre of Excellence (CoE) dedicated to Green Pharma, as the state looks to build a future-ready workforce for AI-driven sustainable manufacturing.

The centre, expected to become operational by August, will train young people in artificial intelligence, sustainable manufacturing, and emerging technologies, supporting the state’s ambition to become a global hub for sustainable pharmaceutical manufacturing under its Next-Gen Life Sciences Policy 2026–30.

The roadmap for the centre was presented to state IT and Industries Minister Duddilla Sridhar Babu. The CoE will include dedicated learning zones focused on Applied AI, Green Pharma, solar energy, electric vehicles, and wind energy. Participants will gain hands-on experience through industry-led projects, innovation cohorts, internships, mentorship, incubation support, and career-readiness programmes.

The Hyderabad facility is one of five Green Skills and Applied AI Centres of Excellence being established across India by Microsoft and the 1M1B Foundation in collaboration with MeitY Startup Hub. Nationally, the initiative aims to engage one lakh youth in Applied AI and Green Skills by 2030 while creating pathways to 50,000 jobs, internships, apprenticeships, and entrepreneurship opportunities.

Speaking on the initiative, Babu said, “Telangana’s next phase of growth would depend on a future-ready workforce capable of leading AI-driven transformation and sustainable innovation in life sciences and advanced manufacturing.”

Highlighting AI’s growing role in sustainable industries, Rajiv Kumar, President and Managing Director, Microsoft India Development Centre, said, “By combining Applied AI with Green Skills, we are preparing a new generation of innovators who can create solutions for both economic growth and climate resilience."

Manav Subodh, Founder and CEO of 1M1B Foundation, said the initiative would prepare young people for the next phase of industrial transformation. “The future of Green Pharma would be built at the intersection of AI, sustainability and human talent.”

Salesforce has launched SMB Growth Kit in India, a bundled offering for small and medium businesses that combines Agentforce Sales, Slack and Tableau into a single platform.

Salesforce said the offering brings customer data, team communication and business analytics together on a single platform, replacing multiple disconnected applications.

The company said businesses adopting the package can go live within four to six weeks through structured onboarding and implementation support.

The package is available immediately and includes onboarding, implementation and post-deployment support. Salesforce said it will deliver the offering through selected reseller partners across India.

According to the company, Agentforce Sales is intended to give SMBs a single view of leads, opportunities and sales pipelines while reducing reliance on spreadsheets and manual recordkeeping.

It includes automated lead assignment, workflow automation, mobile access and AI features such as opportunity scoring, forecasting and recommendations.

Slack serves as the collaboration layer, allowing teams across sales, customer support, HR, IT and operations to work from a single interface. Tableau provides dashboards for tracking pipeline health, revenue trends and business performance using data connected with Salesforce.

“India’s SMBs are moving quickly toward AI, but ambition alone is not enough. Many businesses are investing in AI, but far fewer have implemented it because their customer data, team conversations and business insights are still scattered,” said Mankiran Chowhan, Managing Director, Salesforce India.

“SMB Growth Kit gives growing businesses one connected system where sales activity, team conversations and live insights work together, helping teams act with more confidence, fewer blind spots and less guesswork,” she added.

Swaroop Kaja, RVP, Sales, Salesforce India, said the company built the offering to simplify sales operations and collaboration.

“We launched SMB Growth Kit to give growing businesses one connected way to run sales, collaborate on deals and understand business performance in real time. With Agentforce Sales, Slack and Tableau working together, teams can spend less time chasing updates and more time moving customers forward,” Kaja said.

He added that the combined platform also creates a data foundation for businesses adopting AI as they scale.

The Karnataka government has approved the establishment of a Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence (CoE-AI) at the Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Raichur, under the IT-BT Department’s Local Economy Accelerator Programme (LEAP). The project has been approved with a total outlay of ₹12 crore.

The centre aims to expand AI-driven research, skilling, innovation and entrepreneurship beyond Bengaluru, with a particular focus on tier-2 and tier-3 cities. It is expected to serve as a regional AI hub for North Karnataka while supporting the state’s broader strategy to decentralise technology-led growth.

Announcing the decision, Karnataka IT-BT Minister Priyank Kharge wrote in a LinkedIn post, “The government of Karnataka has approved the establishment of a Centre of Excellence for Artificial Intelligence at the Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Raichur, under the IT-BT Department, Karnataka’s LEAP. With a total outlay of ₹12 crore, this marks another important milestone in our mission to strengthen Karnataka’s AI ecosystem #BeyondBengaluru.”

According to the minister, the CoE will focus on developing practical AI applications across sectors including agriculture, healthcare, education, MSMEs and governance. The initiative is also expected to create opportunities for startups, industry, entrepreneurs and students in North Karnataka.

“The CoE will expand access to AI-driven research, skilling, innovation and entrepreneurship across tier-2 and tier-3 regions while serving as a regional AI hub for North Karnataka,” he stated.

Kharge added that the centre would help strengthen Karnataka’s AI leadership while ensuring that innovation extends beyond the state’s capital.

“More importantly, it will develop practical AI solutions for sectors such as agriculture, healthcare, education, MSMEs and governance while creating new opportunities for industries, entrepreneurs and young innovators. Foundational initiatives like these will strengthen our leadership in AI while ensuring that the next chapter of innovation is written across every region of the State,” Kharge mentioned.

Karnataka’s #BeyondBengaluru initiative seeks to expand the state’s technology ecosystem into emerging innovation hubs by strengthening digital infrastructure, research capabilities and talent development across regions.

Uttar Pradesh is doubling down on its ambitions to become India’s next deep-tech powerhouse, with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directing officials to prepare a comprehensive roadmap for robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), quantum computing, semiconductors, and other emerging technologies. Central to this vision is the development of Park for Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, GPU Clusters and Advanced Technical Innovation (PRAGATI), a 75-acre integrated robotics and advanced manufacturing cluster in Noida, alongside two deep-tech innovation hubs in Noida and Lucknow.

During a review meeting of the Information Technology and Electronics Department, Adityanath said, “The ‘PRAGATI’ project to be developed in Noida will provide the state with a world-class foundation for robotics and advanced manufacturing, while the U Hubs being established in Lucknow and Noida will emerge as major centres of deep tech innovation by bringing research, innovation, startups, industry, investors and educational institutions onto a common platform.”

“Work should be carried out with the objective of making Uttar Pradesh not merely a consumer of new technologies, but a global centre for research, innovation and high-technology-based manufacturing,” he added.

The proposed PRAGATI park, to be developed over approximately 75 acres in Noida, is envisioned as India’s first integrated robotics and advanced manufacturing cluster.

The facility will house a robotics testing and certification centre, rapid prototyping and manufacturing facilities, AI compute infrastructure, GPU clusters, a motion capture lab, a physical AI data centre, startup incubation facilities, and co-working spaces. The project will also bring together global manufacturers, component suppliers, R&D centres, and specialised service providers within a single ecosystem.

According to the government, Noida was selected due to its strong electronics manufacturing base, proximity to Noida International Airport, Jewar, the Dedicated Freight Corridor, the Defence Industrial Corridor, and a well-established industrial and academic ecosystem. The state expects the project to generate over one lakh direct and indirect jobs while contributing more than ₹2,000 crore in gross value addition over the next five years.

Highlighting the broader vision, the Chief Minister said, “Artificial Intelligence and robotics are the principal foundations of the coming industrial revolution. Therefore, while world-class manufacturing infrastructure should be developed on one hand, a strong deep tech ecosystem promoting research, innovation and entrepreneurship should also be created on the other.”

He further stressed the need for collaboration across stakeholders, stating, “An effective coordination mechanism should be established among industry, educational and research institutions, startups, investors and technology experts so that new technologies can rapidly move from laboratories to industry, enabling Uttar Pradesh to emerge as a major hub for global technology investment.”

Complementing the manufacturing cluster, Uttar Pradesh will establish two U Hubs—one each in Noida and Lucknow—with an allocation of ₹100 crore in the 2026–27 state budget. The hubs are intended to function as centres of excellence that connect research institutions, startups, industry, investors, and academia.

The Noida U Hub will focus on quantum computing, semiconductor design, physical AI, robotics, defence technology, and advanced biotechnology, while the Lucknow U-Hub will specialise in applied AI, GovTech, healthcare AI, biosciences, and agri-biotechnology. Their operational framework has been designed by an expert committee chaired by the Director of IIT Kanpur after studying leading global deep-tech ecosystems.

The CM directed that the U Hubs should go beyond being startup workspaces. “A robust platform should be created where technologies developed in research laboratories are commercialised, innovation receives investment, and young people get opportunities to progress from research to entrepreneurship,” he said, adding that the centres should operate “entirely professional, result-oriented and aligned with global best standards.”

Recognising the need for skilled talent, Adityanath also called for large-scale training programmes in AI, machine learning, cybersecurity, cloud computing, semiconductors, and data science.

“Providing the youth of Uttar Pradesh with skills aligned to future technologies is the greatest need of the time,” he said, directing officials to develop world-class training and certification programmes aligned with industry needs through collaboration between educational institutions and industry.

The state also plans to revise its Information Technology Policy to make it more investor-friendly and employment-oriented, while expanding the IT ecosystem beyond Noida and Ghaziabad into tier-2 and tier-3 cities.

“The Information Technology Policy should be made more practical, investor-friendly and employment-oriented in accordance with changing global requirements,” the CM said. “The expansion of the IT industry should not remain confined to Gautam Buddh Nagar and Ghaziabad but should extend to tier-2 and tier-3 cities.”

He added that the policy’s primary objective should be employment generation. “The fundamental objective of the policy should be to create the maximum possible quality employment opportunities for the youth of the state. Local youth should be encouraged in skill development, internships, research, innovation and patents. At the same time, processes related to land, infrastructure and other approvals should be made simple, transparent and time-bound for investors."

The announcements build on Uttar Pradesh’s recent push into AI, semiconductors, and data centres, positioning the state as a destination for high-tech manufacturing and digital infrastructure investments.

The Kolkata facility, TCS’ eighth such centre globally and third in India, is designed to showcase AI-led innovations tailored for consumer business needs and built with Google Cloud and Google’s Gemini models.

According to a statement, the centre will play a critical role in helping enterprises transform their business using TCS’ Human+AI Autonomy model, which will enable organisations to co-create solutions built with Gemini, addressing evolving needs across retail, consumer packaged goods (CPG), and travel, tourism and hospitality (TTH) sectors.

The launch comes as large IT services firms increasingly invest in dedicated AI innovation hubs with hyperscaler partners to move enterprise clients from AI pilots to production deployments.

TCS said it plans to expand the network to 10 Gemini Experience Centers globally by the end of 2026, including four in India.

TCS added that it has built more than 3,000 industry- and context-specific AI agents using Gemini Enterprise, covering industries including consumer goods, retail, travel, transportation and hospitality.

The Kolkata centre adds to TCS’ existing Gemini Experience Centers for retail in Chennai and banking and financial services in Bengaluru, as part of the company’s focus on vertical-specific AI solutions rather than generic deployments.

Roblox has launched Build, an AI-powered game-creation feature that lets users create playable games directly in its mobile app with simple text prompts. The company’s generative AI strategy is now expanding to include not just professional game developers.

Announced on July 16, the new mobile-first creation tab enables users to describe a game idea in natural language, such as “a cosy adventure game set in a dense forest with environmental obstacles”.

It automatically generates a playable starting point complete with gameplay mechanics, environments, characters, visual style and sound. Creators can then refine, test and publish their games without using Roblox Studio or writing code.

The feature, called Build, is powered by Roblox’s proprietary AI models alongside open-source models. The company said the tool is designed to lower the barriers to game development by enabling rapid prototyping and making creation accessible to a wider audience, particularly mobile users.

Build will enter a public alpha on July 28, initially for verified users aged nine and above in New Zealand. Games published through the feature will be playable globally by users aged 16 and older. Roblox said a basic version of the tool will be available free of charge, with premium options planned for advanced creators.

The launch builds on Roblox’s broader AI roadmap. Over the past year, the company has introduced Cube, an open-source AI model for generating 3D objects, followed by 4D creation tools that produce interactive game assets. Earlier this year, Roblox also added agentic AI capabilities to assist developers with planning, building and testing games.

While AI-generated games could increase the volume of content on the platform, Roblox said its existing discovery system will continue to prioritise experiences with strong long-term player engagement rather than automatically promoting AI-created titles.

The company is also developing additional AI agents for playtesting, analytics and monetisation optimisation, which will be integrated into both Build and Roblox Studio in the coming months.

China’s AI startup Moonshot AI has unveiled Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight AI model with a one-million-token context window.

“It is the world’s first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning,” the company said in its blog post.

The model is available through Kimi.com, Kimi Work, Kimi Code and the Kimi API, while its full weights are scheduled for release on July 27.

The Chinese AI startup said Kimi K3 is built on its Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) and Attention Residuals (AttnRes) architectures and includes native vision capabilities.

The company claims the model delivers frontier-level performance in coding, reasoning and knowledge work, although it acknowledged that it still trails proprietary models such as Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol in overall capability.

However, it outperformed OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 and Anthropic’s Opus 4.8 on several benchmarks.

According to Moonshot AI, Kimi K3 is the first open model to reach 2.8 trillion parameters. It uses a mixture-of-experts architecture with 896 experts, activating only 16 experts per token through its Stable LatentMoE framework. The company said the architectural changes improve scaling efficiency by about 2.5 times compared with Kimi K2.

Moonshot AI also highlighted the model’s coding capabilities, saying Kimi K3 can sustain long engineering sessions, navigate large code repositories and use terminal tools with minimal human oversight.

In internal demonstrations, the company said the model built a Triton-like GPU compiler, designed GPU kernels, created browser-based 3D games, edited videos and reproduced computational astrophysics research by reviewing more than 20 papers and generating over 3,000 lines of Python code.

For enterprise users, Moonshot AI introduced two new features in Kimi Work. Widgets generate interactive components inside chats, while Dashboard organises these components into persistent workspaces connected to local data or external plugins.

The company said Kimi K3 currently operates in maximum-thinking mode by default, with low- and high-effort reasoning modes planned for future updates.

HCLTech has expanded its partnership with US-based insurer Guardian Life Insurance Company of America, signing a new seven-year agreement focused on artificial intelligence-led technology and operations modernisation while acquiring the insurer’s India GCC for $10.5 million.

As part of the transaction, HCLTech will acquire 100% of Guardian India Operations, the insurer’s technology and operations GCC, in an all-cash deal expected to close on August 1.

The acquisition will see nearly 2,000 Guardian India employees transition to HCLTech, where they will form a dedicated strategic business unit serving Guardian across technology, engineering and operations.

The engagement comes as IT services companies increasingly deepen client relationships through GCC acquisitions and AI-led transformation programmes, allowing them to secure long-term managed services contracts while gaining specialised industry talent.

Under the agreement, HCLTech will expand deployment of its AI service transformation platform, AI Force, to develop agentic AI capabilities for Guardian and support technology transformation across data, applications and engineering. The companies also plan to jointly develop AI-led products and intellectual property for the insurance industry.

The IT company said the engagement will cover Guardian’s group benefits, individual protection, retirement and wealth management businesses, with the objective of improving operational efficiency, reducing costs and accelerating product delivery.

Guardian’s Chief Digital and Technology Officer, Steve Rullo, said the partnership would help the insurer scale AI adoption across its enterprise while strengthening its operating model.

“Together with HCLTech, we are strengthening how we operate to drive greater consistency and scalability while continuing to invest in the capabilities that differentiate Guardian, strengthen operational excellence, and create value for our customers, policyholders and distribution partners,” Rullo said in a statement.

HCLTech’s Chief Growth Officer and Global Head of Financial Services, Srinivasan Seshadri, said the expanded relationship would enable the companies to co-create AI-led products and strengthen HCLTech’s insurance capabilities.

According to HCLTech’s regulatory filing, Guardian India generated revenue of ₹578.8 crore in FY26, compared with ₹483.2 crore in FY25. The entity, incorporated in 2002, operates as Guardian’s India-based technology and operations GCC, supporting its insurance, retirement and wealth management businesses.

Google has delayed the launch of its flagship Gemini 3.5 Pro model after it failed to meet internal performance targets, particularly in coding, according to a Bloomberg report.

The release, originally expected in June, is now running months behind schedule as the company continues refining the model.

Bloomberg reported that Google has been working to improve Gemini 3.5 Pro’s capabilities before making it publicly available.

The delay comes as competition among AI model developers intensifies, with rivals launching increasingly capable frontier models, including OpenAI’s GPT-5.6, Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Fable 5, Meta’s Muse Spark 1.1, and xAI’s Grok 4.5.

Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai had indicated during Google’s I/O developer conference in May that Gemini 3.5 Pro would be released in June.

However, the model has yet to launch, with engineers continuing to address shortcomings in its performance. Bloomberg reported that Google updated Gemini’s training data in June in an effort to strengthen its coding abilities, but the results fell short of expectations.

The report said the delay has frustrated some employees, who are concerned that Google could lose ground to competitors that have accelerated the pace of model releases in recent months. The company is also balancing the challenge of integrating its AI technology across a broad portfolio of products while improving the underlying model’s capabilities.

The news weighed on investor sentiment, with Alphabet shares falling more than 4% on July 16 as concerns grew that Google may be slipping in the race to deliver leading AI models.

Google has not publicly announced a revised launch date for Gemini 3.5 Pro. Bloomberg reported that the company is prioritising improvements to the model’s quality over meeting its original release timeline.

Databricks has signed a term sheet for fresh funding that values the company at $188 billion, as it steps up investments in enterprise AI products, including Unity AI Gateway, Genie, and Lakebase.

The round, led by existing investor Coatue, is expected to close later this summer and will include both new and existing investors.

The latest financing marks a sharp increase from Databricks’ $134 billion valuation in its previous funding round earlier this year.

The company said it will use the capital to expand its AI offerings, including Unity AI Gateway, which enables enterprises to manage access, governance, and costs across multiple AI models; Genie, its AI assistant for business analytics; and Lakebase, its serverless PostgreSQL database built for AI agents. The funding will also support AI acquisitions and research.

Databricks said many enterprises continue to face a ‘context gap’ that limits AI adoption because business data remains fragmented across systems and is difficult to govern. It said its data and AI platform is designed to bring data and AI together on a single platform while helping organisations manage AI costs, security, and governance.

“Enterprises are moving from tokenmaxxing to valuemaxxing. They don’t want to burn expensive tokens on the smartest model for every task—they want the best outcome per dollar. That means having the freedom to choose the right AI for the job,” said Ali Ghodsi, Co-Founder and CEO of Databricks.

“This new capital lets us keep pushing our multi-AI strategy forward to meet massive customer demand, so we can keep strengthening Unity AI Gateway, expanding Genie, and advancing Lakebase,” he added.

The fundraising comes as Databricks expands beyond its core data platform into AI infrastructure and applications. In recent months, the company has introduced products focused on AI agents and enterprise governance, while positioning Lakebase as a database for agentic AI workloads.

Databricks has also seen strong business growth. The company reported an annual revenue run rate of $5.4 billion earlier this year, with AI products contributing more than $1.7 billion, according to The Wall Street Journal.

The fresh funding is expected to give the company additional firepower to invest in product development and acquisitions without immediate pressure to pursue a public listing.

Wipro reported a muted June-quarter performance, with constant currency revenue rising less than 1% year-on-year and margins contracting, even as the IT services major said artificial intelligence is becoming central to client transformation programmes, helping drive a strong recovery in large deal bookings.

The Bengaluru-headquartered company reported IT services revenue of $2.61 billion for the quarter ended June 30, up 0.9% year-on-year in constant currency but down 1.2% sequentially.

Net profit rose 0.6% year-on-year to ₹3,356 crore, while IT services operating margin narrowed 120 basis points year-on-year to 16.0%.

Large deal bookings stood at $1.62 billion, rising 12.9% sequentially in constant currency, although overall bookings fell 2.4% quarter-on-quarter to $3.37 billion.

The company secured 13 large deals during the quarter.

The company guided for September-quarter IT services revenue in the range of $2.57 billion to $2.63 billion, implying sequential constant currency growth of -1.5% to +0.5%, signalling continued demand uncertainty.

Wipro’s management, however, struck an optimistic note on enterprise AI spending, saying customers are now deploying AI across core business operations rather than limiting it to technology modernisation.

“Clients are moving beyond technology modernisation to AI-enabled operating models that improve quality, resilience, and productivity. Wipro’s consulting-led, AI-powered approach helps clients embed AI at the core of their business, and these engagements reflect both the breadth of our capabilities and the trust clients place in us as a transformation partner,” Srini Pallia, CEO and Managing Director, said in a statement.

The quarter’s largest deal wins reflected that shift. Several engagements are centred on AI-led IT transformation, with Wipro deploying digital agents, AIOps, generative AI and agentic AI capabilities across infrastructure management, software engineering, workplace services and enterprise operations.

Among the key wins, Wipro signed an AI-first transformation programme with a global speciality chemicals company, an AI-native software development modernisation deal with a global technology enterprise, and an engagement with a US hospital network to build an AI and agentic AI roadmap using its WINGS and WEGA platforms. Other large contracts also featured AI-powered automation, intelligent operations and productivity improvements.

Chief Financial Officer Aparna Iyer said the company will continue investing in strategic growth areas despite near-term pressure on profitability.

“As we navigate an evolving technology landscape, we remain focused on investing in our people and strategic priority areas. While these investments may create some near-term margin volatility, they set a strong foundation for future growth,” Iyer said.

Wipro’s voluntary attrition stood at 13.9% on a trailing 12-month basis, while total headcount increased to 2,43,044 employees during the quarter from 2,42,156 in the last quarter.

Tech Mahindra’s investments in artificial intelligenceand higher-value engineering work helped lift profitability in the June quarter, as the IT services company reported a 28.4% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit.

The company on July 16 posted a consolidated net profit of ₹1,465 crore for the first quarter ended June 30, compared with ₹1,141 crore a year earlier. Revenue from operations rose 17.7% to ₹15,712 crore, while EBIT climbed 53.3% to ₹2,264 crore, pushing EBIT margin up 330 basis points to 14.4%.

The quarter adds to a broader trend across India’s IT industry, where companies are increasingly relying on AI-led transformation programmes and higher-value engineering work to improve profitability even as traditional technology spending remains uneven.

New deal wins stood at $1.08 billion, up 33.3% from a year earlier.

Revenue in constant currency grew 6.6% year-on-year and 2.6% sequentially.

Chief Executive Mohit Joshi said the company’s growth reflected stronger client engagement, with the number of customers generating more than $50 million in annual revenue increasing by seven during the quarter, while all business verticals expanded from a year earlier.

“YoY growth of 6.1% coupled with three consecutive quarters of deal wins exceeding $1 billion dollars underscores the resilience of our business and the growing relevance of our offerings,” Joshi said in a statement.

Also, the management indicated it will continue to prioritise AI as an investment area.

“We remain committed to building a future-ready organisation through continued investments in differentiated capabilities, domain-specific and sovereign AI, platforms, and talent—while maintaining a clear focus on growth and operational rigour,” said Chief Financial Officer Rohit Anand.

During the quarter, Tech Mahindra launched an Agentic Development & Modernisation Services portfolio and announced partnerships spanning enterprise AI search, autonomous cloud operations and AI-powered medical writing, as the company broadened its offerings around agentic AI.

It also highlighted multiple client wins in which AI engineering, AIOps and AI-led operations formed a core part of the engagement.

The company ended the quarter with 1,46,760 employees, down 863 sequentially, while IT attrition improved to 11.8% over the last 12 months.

The consumer financing company said the new centre is a nearly 6,000-square-foot facility, making it the company’s third Experience Center worldwide, after two centres in the United States.

The Experience Center allows employees, customers and partners to explore Synchrony’s products, technologies and enterprise capabilities through interactive customer journeys, virtual reality demonstrations and business use cases. The new facilities will also reflect India’s expanding contribution to its global business across technology, operations, analytics, marketing, risk and credit functions. Teams in India develop capabilities including AI-powered productivity tools, cloud-native applications, cybersecurity solutions, analytics platforms and digital experiences that support customers and employees worldwide.

He added that India’s contributions across technology, AI and enterprise platforms continue to strengthen Synchrony’s global capabilities and that the investment reflects the company’s confidence in its India teams.

Rachana Bahadur, SVP and Country Head for India at Synchrony, said the facility was designed for the company’s more than 6,000 colleagues in the country. “It is a place where colleagues can better understand the customers we serve, see the impact of the work they do every day, and come together to learn, connect, collaborate and innovate.”

Synchrony said the Experience Center and Innovation Station will continue to introduce new customer experiences and technologies as its business evolves, serving as a platform for learning, collaboration and innovation.

Thinking Machines Lab, the AI startup founded by former OpenAI Chief Technology Officer Mira Murati, has released Inkling, its first open-weight foundation model.

Inkling is a mixture-of-experts (MoE) transformer with 975 billion total parameters and 41 billion active parameters. The multimodal model supports a context window of up to one million tokens and was pre-trained on 45 trillion tokens spanning text, images, audio and video.

Alongside the flagship model, the company also introduced Inkling-Small, a preview version with 276 billion total parameters and 12 billion active parameters.

“Our mission is to build AI that extends human will and judgment,” the company said in a blog post. “Today we are advancing our mission by releasing a model we trained from scratch with the full weights available, so that people can make it their own.”

Inkling is available on Thinking Machines’ Tinker platform with 64,000-token and 2,56,000-token context options for fine-tuning. The company has also launched an Inkling Playground for developers and is offering the model at a 50% introductory discount for a limited period.

Full model weights have been released on Hugging Face, including an NVFP4 checkpoint optimised for NVIDIA Blackwell systems. The model is also available through Together AI, Fireworks, Modal, Databricks and Baseten, with support for inference frameworks including SGLang, vLLM, TokenSpeed, llama.cpp and Hugging Face Transformers.

Thinking Machines positioned Inkling as a foundation model for customisation rather than a model optimised solely for benchmark leadership.

“Inkling is not the strongest overall model available today, open or closed,” the company said. “Instead, a combination of qualities makes it a good open-weights base for customisation: multimodal capabilities, efficient thinking, and availability on Tinker for fine-tuning.”

Thinking Machines Lab said Inkling is now available for fine-tuning on its Tinker platform to make model customisation accessible across a wider range of use cases.

The model natively supports reasoning across text, images and audio while allowing developers to adjust its reasoning effort to trade off performance, latency and inference cost.

According to the company, Inkling achieves performance comparable to NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3 Ultra on Terminal Bench 2.1 while generating roughly one-third as many tokens. It trails GLM 5.2 and Kimi K2.6 on the benchmark.

Thinking Machines said Inkling was trained on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems and relied on more than 30 million reinforcement learning rollouts during post-training.

The company said reasoning performance improved steadily throughout the reinforcement learning process while the model also learned to produce more concise reasoning traces without affecting final answers.

The company said Inkling was built as a general-purpose model covering reasoning, coding, agentic tool use, instruction following, factuality, vision and audio instead of specialising in a single domain.

It also said the model ranks among the stronger open-weight models on agentic coding benchmarks and Design Arena’s Agentic Web Development leaderboard.

For multimodal tasks, Inkling accepts image and audio inputs without dedicated encoders. The model can transcribe speech, answer questions about recordings, analyse charts and diagrams, and use Python tools for image understanding, including zooming and cropping.

Thinking Machines said it trained Inkling to improve factual calibration, instruction following and resistance to censorship. The company also said external safety testing found the model performed well on benchmarks measuring refusal of harmful requests while avoiding unnecessary refusals of benign prompts.

Madhya Pradesh is stepping up its pitch to become a hub for semiconductors, AI infrastructure, electronics manufacturing, and data centres. Chief Minister, MP Mohan Yadav held a series of one-on-one meetings at MP Tech Growth Conclave 3.0in Bhopal with global and domestic technology companies that together explored investment proposals worth more than ₹58,000 crore.

The discussions spanned semiconductor fabrication, AI-powered data centres, electronics manufacturing, energy storage, solar equipment, and high-performance computing (HPC), reinforcing the state's ambition to emerge as a next-generation technology and manufacturing destination.

Among the largest proposals came from Submer India Private Limited, which expressed interest in investing ₹19,000 crore to develop data centre infrastructure in the state. Discussions focused on land allocation in the Acharpura industrial area and the development of supporting infrastructure.

Another major proposal came from JSM Datacorp Private Limited, which explored the possibility of bringing ₹11,000 crore in foreign direct investment (FDI) for a large-scale data centre project. The discussions covered land availability, power supply, water resources, stamp duty concessions, and incentives under the state's data centre policy.

In the semiconductor sector, Paras Semiconductors proposed investing approximately ₹6,200 crore to establish a semiconductor manufacturing facility on nearly 50 acres in Indore, a project expected to generate around 7,500 jobs. Discussions also covered power supply, industrial infrastructure, and project implementation support.

Thomson Semiconductors also outlined plans to invest around ₹5,200 crore in a semiconductor manufacturing unit in Madhya Pradesh, creating an estimated 2,500 jobs. The discussions focused on land allocation, project approvals, and industrial support.

The state also received a proposal from Nyobolt Ltd. (NBAIDC) to invest around ₹10,000 crore in advanced energy storage technologies, AI data centres, and high-capacity battery manufacturing. The company indicated the project could create 1,300 jobs, while discussions centred on land, power, water, road connectivity, and digital infrastructure.

In electronics manufacturing, Arsenal Infosolutions Pvt. Ltd. proposed an investment of ₹322 crore, with plans to generate nearly 2,240 jobs under an Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) project.

The company sought 30 acres of land along with capital subsidies, electricity concessions, interest subsidies, and additional industrial incentives.

Emerald Infra Ispat Ltd. discussed plans to invest approximately ₹350 crore to establish an electronics manufacturing facility in Bhopal focused on data switches and advanced electronic equipment.

Meanwhile, Osel Devices Limited proposed investing around ₹50 crore in an electronics manufacturing unit expected to create 100–200 jobs, while Fujiyama Power presented plans to invest ₹695.35 crore in solar energy equipment and electronics manufacturing, creating nearly 1,000 jobs.

The state also engaged with Data Oasis LLC (HarmoniQ Data Pvt. Ltd.), which proposed investing around ₹450 crore to establish a hyperscale data centre in Indore over 20 acres, with the project expected to create around 2,000 jobs.

Beyond investment discussions, the Chief Minister also met with NVIDIA Director – Strategic & Business, Ganesh Mahabala, to explore collaboration on strengthening Madhya Pradesh's AI ecosystem.

The discussions covered AI research and innovation, AI skilling, high-performance computing infrastructure, startup ecosystem development, industry-academia partnerships, and the deployment of AI-driven solutions across industry, education, and digital governance.

During the meetings, the Chief Minister assured investors of full government support, highlighting Madhya Pradesh's investor-friendly policies, industrial infrastructure, and fast-track approvals. He said the state is positioning itself as a preferred destination for semiconductor manufacturing, AI infrastructure, electronics production, and large-scale digital infrastructure projects.

content:
OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol has achieved the highest score in ReactBench, a newly introduced benchmark designed to evaluate AI coding agents on realistic React development tasks rather than synthetic programming problems.

The benchmark, released by the team behind React Doctor and React Scan, measures whether models can both implement new React features and fix existing code without introducing performance, accessibility or maintainability issues.

It evaluated GPT-5.6 through Codex CLI, Claude models through Claude Code, GLM 5.2 through GLM CLI and Kimi K2.7 Code through Kimi Code.

Across the benchmark’s 51 curated tasks, GPT-5.6 Sol achieved a pass@1 score of 43%, narrowly ahead of Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 at 41%.

Unlike conventional coding benchmarks, ReactBench does more than verify test-suite results. It also uses React Doctor, an open-source verifier with more than 400 rules that cover React-specific correctness, performance, accessibility and maintainability.

Models must pass hidden behavioural tests without introducing new React Doctor issues.

The researchers said the benchmark remains challenging for current frontier models. Even GPT-5.6 Sol’s best configuration solved fewer than half of all benchmark tasks.

They also cautioned that “the differences among the leading configurations are too small to identify a clear winner with confidence”, despite GPT-5.6 Sol recording the highest observed score.

The report also compared inference costs. Across evaluated configurations, Claude Fable 5 averaged approximately $7.97 per rollout, compared with $1.37 for GPT-5.6 Sol, making Fable about 5.8 times more expensive on average.

The authors highlighted GPT-5.6 Terra as offering the strongest cost-performance trade-off, scoring 38% while costing roughly one-third as much as Sol’s highest-performing configuration.

Beyond ranking models, the benchmark analyses the kinds of mistakes coding agents make. Across 4,455 ‘Write React’ trials, the evaluated models introduced 1,194 graded React issues, with bugs, including security-related findings, accounting for 77.5% of them.

The most common errors involved incorrect list rendering and misuse of React Hooks. The study also found that models typically failed differently depending on the task: feature implementation tasks were more likely to fail behavioural tests, while refactoring tasks more often passed functionality tests but introduced new React quality issues.

ReactBench’s dataset is built from merged pull requests across open-source React repositories. The released version contains 51 tasks derived from more than 23,000 candidate pull requests after automated filtering, manual review and validation.

To reduce potential benchmark contamination, most tasks were sourced from repositories with fewer than 20,000 GitHub stars and from pull requests merged after February.

OpenAI’s new GPT-5.6 Pro (Sol) has helped solve a 20-year-old open problem in statistics by producing a proof that overturns a long-held belief about one of the field’s most widely used statistical methods.

The result appears in a paper by University of Pennsylvania statistician Edgar Dobriban, who said GPT-5.6 Pro generated the proof after being asked to prove or disprove an open question involving the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure, a statistical technique used to reduce false positives when researchers run thousands or even millions of hypothesis tests.

The method is widely used in genomics, biology, medicine, economics and other data-intensive fields.

For nearly two decades, many statisticians believed the method would continue to work even when the underlying tests were correlated.

Dobriban’s paper shows that this is not always true. It presents a mathematical counterexample demonstrating that, under specific conditions, the procedure can produce slightly more false discoveries than its theoretical limit permits.

According to the paper, GPT-5.6 Pro was given only the mathematical definition of the procedure and asked to prove or disprove the claim.

After about 90 minutes of reasoning, the model produced a proof, a counterexample and code to verify the result. Dobriban said he independently checked the entire proof and the accompanying numerical calculations before publishing the work.

“The proof was obtained by GPT-5.6 Pro,” the paper states. It adds that the author “carefully checked the entire argument and the associated numerical certificate” before preparing the final manuscript.

The paper also includes computer simulations that support the theoretical result. While the failure is small, the finding overturns a widely accepted assumption in statistics and raises new questions about the limits of the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure under complex correlations.

The US government only recently lifted restrictions on the public release of OpenAI’s GPT-5.6, clearing the way for the company to make its latest AI model broadly available after weeks of limited access under a government review process.

The GPT-5.6 family consists of three models: the flagship GPT-5.6 Sol model, GPT-5.6 Terra as the mid-tier offering, and GPT-5.6 Luna as the lower-cost option.

The US government initially ordered OpenAI to restrict GPT-5.6 to a small group of government-approved partners while federal agencies evaluated the model’s capabilities and potential cybersecurity risks.

content:
The ESA has chosen Keysight and Sateliot for a three-year project to secure 5G non-terrestrial networks using blockchain technology.

The initiative aims to establish a secure trust framework for satellite-based communications, funded by ESA’s ARTES programme.

The European Space Agency (ESA) has selected Keysight Technologies and Sateliot to develop a blockchain-enabled framework for securing 5G non-terrestrial networks (NTN). The three-year programme will be led by Keysight as the prime contractor, with Sateliot supporting technical development and satellite mission integration.

The project is being funded under ESA’s Advanced Research in Telecommunications Systems (ARTES) programme and aims to create a secure trust framework for satellite-based communications.

The initiative will explore how blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and digital calibration certificates can be used across the satellite lifecycle, from manufacturing and testing to in-orbit operations and service delivery.

Antonio Franchi, Head of ESA’s Space for 5G/6G & Sustainable Connectivity programme, said the project would help develop technologies needed to secure future communications networks.

“The future of Europe’s connectivity depends on networks that are not only advanced but trusted, resilient and secure,” Franchi said. He added that the programme would help protect communications against spoofing and tampering while supporting Europe’s position in secure 5G and future 6G communications.

As satellite constellations expand, interactions between satellites, ground systems, and terrestrial 5G networks are increasing. ESA said this is creating challenges related to network security, anomaly management, service quality, and operational confidence. The agency believes trusted and verifiable data will become critical as 6G networks incorporate greater non-terrestrial infrastructure and autonomous operations.

According to Keysight, the programme will progress from laboratory research and prototyping to a full in-orbit demonstration. The companies plan to validate blockchain-based trust mechanisms, autonomous anomaly detection, and secure telemetry in operational satellite environments.

Eric Taylor, Vice President of Aerospace, Defence and Government Solutions at Keysight, said the initiative comes as non-terrestrial network deployments accelerate globally.

“By combining test and measurement expertise with AI-driven assurance and blockchain technologies, this work will demonstrate how trust can be embedded across the full NTN lifecycle, from design and validation through in-orbit operation,” Taylor said.

ESA said the programme is expected to inform future non-terrestrial network operations, support secure satellite connectivity, and contribute to the adoption of trusted space-based 5G and 6G networks worldwide.

Bengaluru-based biotech startup Mandrake Bio has raised approximately ₹16 crore in a pre-seed funding round co-led by Activate and Antler, as it looks to develop programmable gene-editing enzymes designed from scratch using AI.

The round also saw participation from Spectrum Impact and DeVC, along with angel investors including Dr Vijay Chandru, Paras Chopra, Sanjiv Rangrass, and Vatsal Dusad.

The company said it will use the capital to further develop its AI-based protein design platform, grow its research team across AI and biophysics, and scale wet-lab validation of gene editors for agricultural and medical applications.

Mandrake Bio is building gene-editing enzymes that it says are smaller and tailored for specific use cases. The company combines generative AI with biophysics to design proteins from scratch before testing them in the laboratory.

Current gene-editing tools such as CRISPR-Cas9 face limitations in both agriculture and medicine, according to the company. In agriculture, conventional breeding can take 10 to 15 years to introduce a new trait into commercial crop varieties, while gene editing can reduce that timeline to one or two years.

Existing editors often require tissue culture, which adds time and infrastructure requirements. In medicine, approved gene-editing therapies are largely ex vivo and can cost millions of dollars per patient, while in vivo approaches remain constrained by delivery challenges and the size of existing editing enzymes.

Mandrake said its approach is aimed at overcoming these constraints by designing compact, programmable editors for specific applications rather than relying on naturally occurring proteins.

The company also pointed to its recent performance at the GEM × Adaptyv RBX1 protein design competition held during ICLR Rio 2026. According to Mandrake, its protein design engine generated the only submission rated ‘Strong’ among more than 12,000 entries.

Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Bengaluru, Mandrake Bio was established by Tanay Lohia and Dr Kutubuddin Molla.

Lohia previously led carbon-credit and climate resilience programmes at Absolute before joining AI research lab Lossfunk, where he developed the foundation for Mandrake.

Molla, a senior scientist at ICAR-CRRI, is among the first researchers to demonstrate the compact gene editor TnpB in plants.

“We’ve always been limited by the tools we discovered in nature. At Mandrake, we use generative AI and biophysics to design proteins from scratch instead, so that improving a crop needn’t take a decade, and a transformative therapy needn’t cost millions,” said Lohia, CEO of Mandrake Bio.

“Our designs already stand among the best in the world, and they're coming out of India. This is the chapter where we start writing biology, not just reading it,” he added.

Pratyush Choudhury, Co-founder of Activate, said AI's next wave of impact would extend beyond software into fields such as biology, chemistry and materials science.

“We believe India has the talent to build companies at that frontier. Mandrake is a great example: combining world-class AI with deep biological science to create entirely new gene editing tools from first principles,” Choudhury said.

Nitin Sharma, Partner at Antler, said the startup is addressing a core challenge in gene editing by combining AI, biophysics and laboratory validation.

Applied Computing has secured $20 million in funding led by KBR to expand its AI solutions for the energy sector.

The company plans to establish a presence in the US with a new office in Houston, Texas.

British industrial AI startup Applied Computing has raised $20 million in a funding round led by engineering and technology firm KBR, with Databricks Ventures joining as a new investor, as the company looks to expand its AI platform for energy operators globally.

The company also announced its entry into the US market by opening a new office in Houston, Texas. Headquartered in London, Applied Computing operates an engineering and operations hub in Bengaluru, India, as well as a new US presence.

The fresh capital will be used to accelerate international expansion, expand its research and engineering teams, and deepen commercial deployments of Orbital, the company’s flagship foundation AI model built specifically for energy operations.

Unlike general-purpose AI models, Orbital combines physics-grounded intelligence with chemical engineering, time-series forecasting, and language models to help energy operators improve efficiency, reduce emissions, strengthen reliability, and optimise decision-making across upstream, downstream, and petrochemical operations.

“It’s our mission to provide operators with a foundation model that unlocks advantage at scale while delivering pathways to production that are safer, more efficient and far less carbon intensive. KBR is a natural partner for that mission,” Callum Adamson, CEO and Co-Founder of Applied Computing, said in a statement.

Greg Conlon, Chief Digital and Development Officer at KBR, said the investment would strengthen the company’s AI capabilities across its technology portfolio. “Together, we’re redefining how AI powers the critical systems that drive global economic growth,” he said.

Julien Debard, Director of Energy and Utilities at Databricks, said the company decided to invest after seeing “how quickly operators can now move from experimentation to real operational value on the platform”.

The funding follows a series of commercial partnerships with KBR, Databricks and Wipro. Applied Computing also said it has signed a multi-year agreement with KBR to jointly develop exclusive AI products for the energy sector and plans to announce its first partnership with a European oil major in the coming weeks.

Zoho has launched Zoho Classes 2.0, an AI-powered learning management system (LMS) that will be offered free of product licensing costs to all central and state government schools, colleges, and universities in India. The company will also provide the platform free to individual teachers handling up to 100 students, as it looks to expand access to AI-enabled education technology.

The platform, built in India and launching first in the country before expanding globally, combines AI-powered teaching, student lifecycle management, institutional intelligence, and multilingual support into a single academic platform. Zoho said the LMS supports all 22 scheduled Indian languages, enabling AI-generated teaching content, assessments, and learning materials in regional languages.

The announcement comes as educational institutions increasingly look to integrate artificial intelligence into teaching and administration while aligning with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and outcome-based education frameworks.

“Education shapes how societies learn, adapt, and grow, making it one of the most important areas where technology can create lasting impact. Every education system is unique, and technology must be built around local needs and diverse learning environments. This belief has shaped Zoho Classes into a platform designed to adapt to the diverse students and education systems it serves,” said Mani Vembu, CEO of Zoho.

Vembu added that the company wanted to democratise access to educational technology by removing licensing costs for public institutions.

“We believe access to modern educational technology should never be limited by an institution’s resources. As part of our commitment to democratising access, Zoho Classes are being made available at no product licensing cost to central and state government schools, colleges, and universities across India. We hope this enables more institutions to harness technology to improve learning outcomes and expand educational opportunities,” he said.

Zoho Classes 2.0 introduces three major capabilities: AI embedded throughout the learning journey, student engagement tools designed for digital-native learners, and institutional intelligence for administrators.

Among its key AI features is an AI Course Builder, which can generate a structured course—including lesson plans, assignments, assessments, and outcome mapping—from a syllabus or topic in under 30 seconds. The platform also includes a 24/7 AI tutor for students, adaptive assessments, gamified learning, and microlearning modules.

For educational institutions, the platform provides student lifecycle management from enrolment to graduation, while AI identifies at-risk students and recommends intervention opportunities. Administrators can also track student outcomes, engagement trends, and operational performance through built-in analytics dashboards.

“Traditional LMS platforms were built to deliver academic content, not experiences. But today’s students, raised on short-form video and instant feedback, expect learning to be interactive and immersive, and traditional formats no longer hold their attention,” said Dev Anand Ramasamy, Vice President of Product Management, Zoho.

“At the same time, institutions need to improve outcomes without adding to teachers’ load. That is the gap we set out to bridge. Zoho Classes 2.0 uses a deeply embedded AI layer to automate time-intensive work like lesson planning, grading, and reporting, freeing teachers to focus on what matters most: teaching and engaging students,” he added.

Zoho said the platform has been built to support India’s multilingual education landscape and is already working with government education bodies on digital learning initiatives spanning government schools, polytechnic colleges, and statewide education networks.

The platform also supports outcome-based education (OBE) and accreditation requirements for NAAC, NBA, UGC, NMC, and competency-based medical education workflows required by the National Medical Commission.

Built on Zoho’s vertically integrated technology stack, the platform offers data residency in India and complies with the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act.

According to the company, Zoho Classes has already delivered over eight million notifications, supported more than one million assignment submissions, enabled over 1,00,000 minutes of learning content consumption, and hosts more than 2 TB of teacher-created video content. The platform is currently used by institutions including SRM Institute, Sishya School, Chettinad Health City, CGIHM, Vidya Mandir, Grace International School, GSE Institute, as well as government education bodies.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has launched an AI engineering lab in Bengaluru in partnership with NVIDIA, betting on growing enterprise demand for industrial artificial intelligence applications in manufacturing, mobility and autonomous systems.

Located at TCS’ Global Axis campus, the TCS Autonomous Engineering Lab is designed as a physical AI facility where enterprises can prototype, simulate, test and validate AI applications before deploying them in live industrial environments.

The move comes as technology services firms increasingly expand beyond AI consulting into dedicated infrastructure and engineering capabilities to help clients operationalise AI at scale.

The lab will leverage NVIDIA’s AI infrastructure and TCS’ industrial engineering capabilities to develop applications spanning software-defined vehicles, autonomous driving, digital twins, smart manufacturing and agentic AI, the company said.

“As we move forward into our next phase and deepen our collaboration, we will build on this momentum into scaled deployment and enterprise-wide transformation for more customers, with confidence and speed,” Sreenivasa Chakravarti, Global Head and Vice President of Industrial Autonomy and Engineering, TCS, said in a statement.

According to the company, the lab will support customers in integrating AI into products, manufacturing plants and industrial operations, with use cases including predictive maintenance, automated quality inspection, real-time process optimisation and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). It will also provide access to NVIDIA’s AI ecosystem and computing infrastructure for testing and validation.

“As enterprises push to operationalise AI across physical operations, they require specialised infrastructure to bridge the gap between simulation and real-world deployment. Through this collaboration, the TCS Industrial Autonomy and Engineering Lab leverages the full-stack NVIDIA AI platform to offer customers a scalable pathway for validating and implementing their next-generation industrial solutions,” Alvin DaCosta, Vice President, AI Consulting Partners, NVIDIA, said.

The announcement marks an expansion of the longstanding partnership between TCS and NVIDIA beyond technology integration to include joint capability building, customer engagement and solution development.

Spain-based Submer Group has announced a $2 billion (approximately ₹19,000 crore) investment in Madhya Pradesh’s semiconductor sector, marking one of the state’s largest commitments in advanced technology manufacturing. The project is expected to generate nearly 5,000 direct jobs as the state officials mentioned to AIM.

Furthermore, it is the culmination of the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed between the Madhya Pradesh State Electronics Development Corporation (MPSEDC) and Spain-based Submer Technologies in July 2025.

In addition to the semiconductor project, Submer Group has sought land for a data centre, with the government allotting 15 acres in the Acharpura Industrial Area within six days of the company’s request.

The rapid land allocation underscores the state’s push to fast-track strategic technology investments amid increasing competition among Indian states to attract semiconductor and AI infrastructure projects.

Submer Group, headquartered in Spain, serves major cloud and digital infrastructure customers globally and has been expanding its manufacturing footprint to meet rising demand driven by artificial intelligence and hyperscale data centres. With the latest investment, Madhya Pradesh joins a growing list of states seeking to establish themselves as destinations for semiconductor manufacturing, AI infrastructure, and data centre investments as India’s electronics and digital economy continues to expand.

US AI startup PrismML has unveiled Bonsai 27B, an open-source multimodal language model that it says is the first model in the 27-billion-parameter class to run on a smartphone, marking its latest attempt to bring larger AI models to consumer devices.

The California-based startup said Bonsai 27B is built on Alibaba’s Qwen3.6 27B model and is available in two versions. The ternary variant occupies 5.9 GB and uses 1.71 effective bits per weight, while the 1-bit version requires 3.9 GB with 1.125 effective bits per weight, making it small enough to fit within the memory constraints of modern smartphones.

Both models are available under the Apache 2.0 licence.

At the same time, Apple has been evaluating PrismML’s model compression technology to run larger AI models directly on iPhones, according to a CNBC report.

A conventional 27B model requires about 54 GB of memory in FP16 precision, while a typical 4-bit quantised version still occupies around 18 GB, making local deployment difficult on phones and many laptops, the company said.

“Bonsai 27B is the new multimodal flagship of the Bonsai family,” PrismML said. “Based on Qwen3.6 27B, it brings a new capability tier to local AI: multi-step reasoning, structured tool use, long-context workflows, and coherent agentic loops.”

According to the company, both variants support multimodal inputs, a 2,62,000-token context window, speculative decoding and end-to-end low-bit execution across the model without reverting to higher-precision layers.

PrismML said the ternary version retains about 95% of the full-precision model's performance across a 15-benchmark suite, while the 1-bit version retains roughly 90%.

The startup said the release is intended for local AI workloads such as reasoning, coding, tool use and agentic workflows that can run without depending entirely on cloud infrastructure.

“Bonsai 27B changes that,” the company said, referring to the memory requirements of existing models. “Cloud APIs will remain the right choice for many products. What has been missing is a model small enough to deploy this way and capable enough to be trusted with the work.”

Founded in 2026 as a spinout from the California Institute of Technology by Babak Hassibi, Sahin Lale, Omead Pooladzandi and Reza Sadri, PrismML has raised $16.25 million in seed funding from Khosla Ventures, Cerberus Ventures and Caltech.

The company also counts Google as a backer and receives continuing support from Samsung. Earlier this year, it introduced the Bonsai 8B family, applying similar low-bit techniques to smaller language models.
